description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott Undergraduate Internship   Programme   
 

 Unlock Your Potential at Abbott   

 Looking for an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge, gain hands-on experience, and make a real impact? Abbott's Undergraduate Internship   Programme   offers students the chance to work on meaningful projects, collaborate with industry experts, and contribute to innovations that help people live healthier lives.   
 

 As an Abbott intern,   you'll   gain practical experience in a global healthcare   organisation , develop sought-after skills, and build a strong professional network. Whether your interests lie in Engineering, Science, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, IT, or other STEM disciplines,   you'll   be supported to learn, grow, and reach your potential.   
 

 Many of our interns go on to secure Graduate opportunities, Professional Development   Programme   positions, and long-term careers across Abbott's sites in Ireland and around the world.   
 

 What You Can Expect   

 As an Abbott intern,   you'll   gain hands-on experience while working on meaningful projects that contribute to healthcare innovation. Depending on your area of study and placement, you may support engineering, manufacturing, scientific, quality, supply chain, business, or technology initiatives that make a real impact.    
 

 What's   in it for you?   

 Apply your academic learning in a real-world environment.   

 
 Gain valuable hands-on experience with a global healthcare leader.   

 
 Contribute to   meaningful projects that help   people live healthier   lives.   

 
 Learn from experienced professionals and receive ongoing mentorship.   

 
 Develop technical, professional, and leadership capabilities.   

 
 Build your network across Abbott's Ireland operations.   

 
 Gain exposure to diverse functions, projects, and career paths.   

 
 Benefit from 6, 9, or 12-month internship opportunities aligned to your academic   programme .   

 
 Explore future opportunities through Abbott's Graduate   Programmes   and long-term career pathways.   

 

 Placement length and location will vary depending on business requirements and academic   programme   requirements.   

   

 About Abbott   

 Abbott is a global healthcare   leader   developing life-changing technologies that help people live healthier lives. With more than 122,000 colleagues serving people in over 160 countries, we deliver innovative solutions across diagnostics, medical devices, nutrition, and medicines.   
 

 In Ireland, Abbott employs more than 6,200 people across ten sites, providing interns with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in world-class STEM and business environments while contributing to healthcare innovation.   
 

 Employment offers are subject to the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening.   
 

 Why Choose Abbott?   

 At Abbott,   you'll   gain hands-on experience, work on meaningful projects, and develop skills that will support your future career.   You'll :   

 Contribute to healthcare innovations that improve lives.   

 
 Learn from experienced professionals and industry experts.   

 
 Build valuable skills and expand your professional network.   

 
 Gain exposure to opportunities across Abbott's Ireland network, with flexibility to be based at different Abbott locations.   

 
 Explore future career opportunities within Abbott.   

 

 Our internship   Programme   provides real-world experience, broad exposure, and   a strong foundation   for future career growth.   
 

 Area of Opportunity   

 Depending on business needs and your area of study, you may have the opportunity to gain experience in one or more of the following areas:   
 

 Information Technology (IT)   

 Supporting digital transformation, data analytics, cybersecurity, and technology   initiatives that help drive innovation, enhance business performance, and enable Abbott to deliver life-changing healthcare solutions worldwide.   
 

 Specific assignments will be aligned to business requirements, site needs, and individual development opportunitie s   
 

 What You'll Bring   

 At Abbott,   we're   looking for students with   the curiosity , drive, and ambition to make a difference. Successful candidates will:   

 Be available for a 6, 9, or 12-month placement aligned with their academic   program me .   

 
 B e pursuing an undergraduate or postgraduate qualification in   Engineering, Technology or   another   relevant STEM discipline 

 
 Be on track to achieve, or have achieved, a minimum   2.1 degree   classificatio n.   

 
 Bring   strong communication , teamwork, and analytical skills.   

 
 Demonstrate initiative, curiosity, and   a desire   to learn.   

 
 Have   a passion for innovation, STEM, and healthcare.   

 
 Thrive in a collaborative environment and be willing to take ownership of their work.   

 

 Have flexibility to be based at any Abbott Ireland location, providing opportunities for broader exposure, diverse experiences, and professional growth.

Job Description:
Role Purpose
The purpose of the role is to provide effective technical support to the process and actively resolve client issues directly or through timely escalation to meet process SLAs.
Responsibilities:
Deal Management: Collaborate closely with ABF Deal Analysts to assist in investment management and monitoring activities for structured finance deals.
IC Memos: Support the deal team in updating Investment Committee approval memos, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of each deal's intricacies.
Term sheets: Analyze closing documents such as credit agreements, indentures and note purchase agreements and set up processes for analyzing and monitoring the deal post-closing.
Due Diligence: Perform pre-deal due diligence and stratify the collateral pool using Python to assess risk and investment potential.
Surveillance and Reporting: Update surveillance data and create one-pagers for presentations to senior management for both Public and Private deals.
Cashflow Modeling: Develop and update cashflow models for structured finance deals. Monitor key metrics to assess risk and expected returns. Conduct stress case scenarios and analyze their impact on repayments.
Collateral Analysis: Create and update asset-level one-pagers for collateral analysis, assisting in underwriting and post-deal monitoring.
Asset Valuation: Track and review revaluation events for underlying assets, ensuring accurate pricing of collateral.
Sector-Level Analysis: Update monthly sector-level presentations and pro-actively highlight potential issues to senior management.
Covenant Monitoring: Continuously monitor covenants and key performance indicators (KPIs) at the deal level, thereby assist the Business Analytics team to run portfolio-level analysis.
Ad Hoc Projects: Undertake multiple ad hoc projects as requested by senior management to assess the impact of macro events.
Client request/ Compliances: Ensure compliance with investor requirements from an investment management perspective.
Data and Tools: Leverage advanced tools such as Intex and Python for in-depth analysis. Utilize Tableau, Street Diligence and Sigma for enhanced data visualization.

MBA in Finance, CFA, or CA qualification.
Experience in analyzing Asset Backed Finance deal structures and collateral is a plus.
Strong analytical and quantitative skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools (MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, and MS Word).
Ability to summarize complex information succinctly and efficiently.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

title: Module Engineer Internship
description:
Job Details: 
 
 Job Description:  Step into the world of advanced semiconductor manufacturing and help shape the future of technology. At Intel Ireland, we're not just building semiconductor chips, we're building the future.
 
 As a Module Engineering Intern, you'll join a team of passionate engineers working on Intel's most advanced process technologies. You'll gain hands-on experience in a high-tech, fast-paced environment where innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning are at the heart of everything we do.

This internship is your opportunity to apply your STEM education in a real-world setting, working alongside experienced engineers to solve complex problems, optimize manufacturing processes, and contribute to the development of world-changing technology.

 Responsibilities / What You'll Do 
 Responsible for safety, quality, operational performance, and improving productivity in addition to cost reduction for their module.

 Ownership and qualification of process modules and/or equipment, including Preventative Maintenance, Root Cause analysis, Monitoring Process Performance, and Defect Reduction

 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve technical challenges using structured, model-based problem-solving techniques.

 Contribute to sustaining and improving Intel's Virtual Factory standards and process matching across global sites.

 Engage in continuous learning and development through mentorship and training.

 
 
 Qualifications: Minimum Requirements: 
 Currently pursuing a Level 8 or Level 9 qualification in a relevant STEM discipline (e.g. Physics, Applied Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, etc.).

 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

 Excellent communication skills - both written and verbal.

 Ability to work independently and as part of a diverse, high-performing team.

 Willingness to work in a cleanroom environment.

 Strong attention to detail and disciplined approach to procedures.

 
 Preferred Experience:
 Experience with data analysis tools and software (e.g. JMP, Python, Excel).

 Ability to summarize data for technical and non-technical audiences.

 
 What We Offer
 A dynamic, inclusive, and innovative work environment.

 Hands-on experience with cutting-edge semiconductor technology.

 Mentorship from experienced engineers and opportunities to grow your technical and professional skills.

 Exposure to Intel's global manufacturing operations and Virtual Factory model.

 The chance to contribute to meaningful projects that impact the lives of every person on the planet.

 
 You must also be available for six+ months in 2027 with a preferred starting date between January and June 2027. 
 
           
 
 
 Job Type: Student / Intern 
 
 Shift: Shift 1 (Ireland) 
 
 Primary Location:  Ireland, Leixlip 
 
 Additional Locations:

Position of Trust N/A  
 EU Salary We offer a total compensation package that ranks among the best in the industry. 
The minimum Annual Salary for this job which could be performed in Ireland is: €31,400.00

As part of our total compensation approach, the final offer may also include additional pay components and benefits. Salary: €34,500
This role is being offered as a 23-month contract
Ready to start your career at AIB?
Join an award-winning graduate programme with AIB, recognised by gradireland as the ‘Most Popular Graduate Recruiter in Banking, Investment & Financial Services’ for six consecutive years and a winner of the Diversity Recruitment Award.
Help shape the transition to a more sustainable future.
As a Group Sustainability Graduate at AIB, you'll work on initiatives that support customers, businesses and communities in responding to some of the most important challenges of our time, including climate change, sustainable finance and environmental transition.
You'll develop valuable research, analytical and stakeholder management skills while helping AIB deliver on its sustainability ambitions and support the transition to a more sustainable economy.
At AIB, we know that starting your career is a big step. That's why we've created a graduate programme that gives you meaningful work, plenty of support and opportunities to develop both professionally and personally.
Over 23 months, you'll gain exposure to a wide range of sustainability initiatives, work on impactful projects and develop the skills, experience and confidence needed to build a successful career.
No two days will be the same!
Why join our graduate programme?
As part of the programme, you'll contribute to and learn from Group Sustainability activities across AIB while building expertise within a dedicated team.
You'll learn on the job, contribute to real business initiatives and work alongside experienced professionals who are invested in helping you succeed.
Along the way, you'll also have opportunities to:
Build your professional network
Attend development events
Connect with senior leaders across the organisation
Learn from graduates who have already completed the programme
Explore different career paths within AIB
Work on issues that matter to people, communities and the environment
This is more than a graduate programme. It's an opportunity to contribute to meaningful work while building the knowledge and skills needed to support a more sustainable future.
What You’ll Do
Sustainability is transforming the banking industry. Understanding how environmental, social and economic trends impact customers, businesses and financial markets helps shape better decisions and supports the transition to a more sustainable future.
At AIB, sustainability is central to our strategy. Our Group Sustainability team plays an important role in generating insights that help shape business decisions, support customers and embed sustainability into how we operate.
As a Sustainability Graduate, you'll help generate insights that support AIB's sustainability strategy and assist customers in navigating the transition to a more sustainable economy.
Your work will contribute to initiatives that support responsible banking, sustainable finance and long-term value creation for customers and communities.
What's in it for you?
Alongside valuable experience and development opportunities, you'll enjoy:
21 days annual leave plus 2 additional volunteer days
Additional AIB Bank Holidays, including Good Friday and the day after St Stephen's Day
Hybrid working with 3 days in the office and 2 days working from home
Exposure to a range of sustainability initiatives and projects
Strong emphasis on wellbeing and work-life balance
Structured learning and development programme
Defined Contribution Pension Scheme
Vhi Healthcare scheme
Variable remuneration scheme
We are with you every step of the way
Starting your first professional role can feel daunting, but we'll be with you every step of the way.
Every graduate is assigned a dedicated People Leader who will support your development, help you navigate challenges and encourage you to get the most from your experience.
You'll also become part of a vibrant graduate community, joining fellow Sustainability graduates as well as graduates from previous intakes. Whether it's learning, networking or social events, you'll quickly build relationships that last well beyond the programme.
We also offer access to a wide range of support networks and initiatives, including our Employee Assistance Programme and Mentor Her programme.
Entry Requirements:
Achieved or expected to achieve a minimum 2.1 Honours Degree (or equivalent for universities outside of Ireland) is a prerequisite for those joining the AIB graduate programme.
Candidates must be fully authorised to work in Ireland or hold a valid work permit for the full duration of the 23-month contract (September 2027 – August 2029).
If you are not sure about your suitability based on any aspects of the role advertised, we encourage you to please contact our Future Talent Programmes team at Grads@aib.ie for a conversation.

title: Delivery Centre – Administrator-Hybrid
description: Deloitte is the world’s number one professional services firm and making an impact is more than what we do. It is why we are here. We bring challenge, curiosity and edge to every project, driving positive progress for our clients, our people, our communities and the planet. This purpose inspires us to work to the highest standards and to tackle the challenges that matter. Number one never stops challenging. Audit and Assurance is one of Deloitte Ireland’s largest service lines and a core engine of our business. As the world’s number one professional services firm, we bring challenge, curiosity and edge to the financial reporting ecosystem. We deliver insight, confidence and value for leading local and international clients. Our teams combine advanced technology with deep professional expertise to evolve our audit and assurance processes. You will work with talented colleagues across our global network to make an impact that matters every day. Number one never stops challenging and neither do we. We offer a competitive starting salary of €29,030.00 for this role, with salary adjustments reflecting your experience level and expertise. . Why you'll enjoy this new opportunity Joining Deloitte’s Delivery Centre (DDC) in Cork means becoming part of a dynamic team that plays a crucial role in supporting Ireland’s audit business. This role offers the chance to contribute to streamlining audit processes, reducing administrative burdens, and enhancing client service quality. You will benefit from Deloitte’s commitment to agile working, professional development, and a collaborative culture that values your input and growth. Key skills and prior experience that align well with this position Experienced in an administrative role within a professional environment Excellent organisational and prioritising skills with strong attention to detail Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with multiple stakeholders Ability to manage multiple tasks under tight deadlines while taking initiative and working collaboratively What type of work will I be doing? Supporting audit teams and managers throughout various stages of the audit lifecycle Preparing, issuing, and acquiring letters requesting audit evidence from external third parties Liaising with audit teams and third parties to resolve queries promptly Preparing reports, letters, and other documents including branding, proofreading, and formatting Providing audit-specific administrative support as required Contributing to the development of best practices and continuous improvement within the DDC Embracing flexible and remote working techniques to support efficient service delivery Who is the Hiring Manager? The hiring manager is an experienced leader within Deloitte’s Irish audit service line, known for a collaborative and supportive leadership style. They value open communication, professional development, and fostering a positive team environment. Their approach balances high standards with empathy, encouraging innovation and continuous learning while maintaining a strong focus on delivering exceptional client service. Where is this role based? This role is based at Deloitte’s Delivery Centre in Cork, Ireland, with a flexible working model that supports agile and remote working arrangements. For more information on our working approach, please visit the Deloitte Works webpage. If you meet most of the criteria above, we encourage you to apply. Deloitte is an equal opportunities employer and will ensure that any reasonable accommodations are implemented throughout the recruitment and selection process. What we offer Your reward at Deloitte is competitive, purpose driven and designed to support your growth. It is more than salary. We invest in your personal and professional development, empower your work life balance and offer benefits that support you at every stage of life. These include health and wellbeing supports, pension and savings options, training and coaching and enhanced leave options. Deloitte is the number one professional services firm in the world, and the leading global provider of audit and assurance, consulting, financial advisory, risk advisory, sustainability, tax, and related services. We have offices across Ireland in Dublin, Belfast, Cork, Limerick and Galway. Deloitte is proud of the enhanced flexibility that we offer our people through our hybrid working strategy, Deloitte Works. It means we trust our people with the flexibility and control to make the right choices in where, when, and how they work. Deloitte is looking for people that have a leadership mindset, are curious, enjoy solving challenges and are eager to grow their careers.

Company Description
ORIX Aviation is an aircraft leasing company established in 1991, currently with over 200 aircraft owned, managed, and committed on lease to more than 50 airlines across greater than 30 countries. ORIX Aviation is also a 30% shareholder in Avolon, one of the world’s largest aircraft lessors. ORIX Aviation has offices in Dublin and Dubai and works closely with a team of aviation specialists in ORIX Corporation in Tokyo. The team consists of 100+ aviation professionals across the three locations. ORIX Aviation is an S&P ranked aircraft servicer and has earned a “strong” ranking - the highest possible ranking - with a stable outlook. ORIX Aviation is positioned to grow both its owned book aircraft as well as managed aircraft in the coming years. ORIX Aviation believes in the power of diversity and is an equal opportunities employer.
Position
Lead the Powerplant function across engine maintenance strategy, shop visit oversight, cost validation, maintenance forecasting, technical risk management, and transaction support. The role is responsible for providing senior technical direction on engine-related matters, protecting asset value, and supporting commercial decisions across the aircraft and engine portfolio.
Lead the planning, coordination, and oversight of major engine maintenance events across the managed fleet.
Develop, review, and challenge engine shop visit workscopes, maintenance strategies, and operator or MRO recommendations.
Assess shop visit proposals to ensure technical necessity, lease alignment, cost control, and protection of asset value.
Review and validate shop visit costs, invoices, maintenance reserve claims, and related supporting documentation.
Maintain engine maintenance forecasts and exposure assumptions in coordination with airlines, MROs, OEMs, and internal stakeholders.
Provide senior technical input to aircraft and engine transitions, including due diligence, delivery readiness, redelivery planning, and execution risk management.
Support LOIs, lease agreements, lease amendments, lease placements, sales, and trading transactions, including review and validation of engine-related rates and assumptions.
Identify, assess, and communicate technical risks that may affect asset value, maintenance exposure, lease economics, transition execution, or transaction outcomes.
Develop and agree practical mitigation actions for engine maintenance, technical, commercial, and transition-related risks.
Act as a senior technical interface with Trading, Marketing, Pricing, Asset Management, Risk, Legal, and Technical teams.
Maintain market awareness through engagement with operators, OEMs, MROs, appraisers, and wider industry contacts.
Provide guidance and oversight to more junior Powerplant or technical team members on data, maintenance, records, and transaction-related matters.
Translate complex technical findings into clear, decision-ready recommendations for commercial, asset management, and senior leadership stakeholders.
Requirements
5-10 years of relevant powerplant, airline, MRO, OEM, leasing, or technical asset management experience preferred.
Relevant university degree or technical qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Aircraft Maintenance, or a related discipline.
Strong understanding of engine maintenance, shop visit management, lease-related maintenance obligations, and aircraft technical records.
Experience reviewing shop visit workscopes, invoices, reserve claims, engine rates, and maintenance exposure assumptions.
Strong commercial awareness with the ability to assess the impact of technical matters on asset value, lease economics, and transaction execution.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical matters clearly to senior internal stakeholders.
Advanced Microsoft Excel capability and confidence working with technical, utilisation, maintenance, and financial data.
Proactive, well-organised, detail-focused, and able to manage competing priorities across maintenance, transactions, and portfolio management.
Aircraft leasing experience desirable.
Other information
Working with ORIX Aviation
Outside of an attractive and competitive remuneration package, and based in a modern office block situated in a desirable location, other benefits of the ORIX Aviation culture include:
A flexible hybrid working model,
A Social Committee who arrange multiple social events; everything from meals out and pub quizzes to family fun days and social drinks
Participation in company sports teams such as tag rugby, tennis and football
Access to on-site gym and subsidised external gym and sport club memberships
Annual fundraising for charities and community organisations
Opportunity to get involved in ORIX Aviation’s committees which include Wellness, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion, ECO and Sports & Social
Secondment opportunities to Dubai
ORIX Aviation is an equal opportunities employer and accepts applications from people of all backgrounds and disciplines. title: Insight Analyst
description:
Because we strive to put people first.

Culture, our way.
 Technology at Primark 
 What’s a career at Primark all about? The positive impact you’re making, the experiences you’re having and the people you’re with. You’re our inspiration. Embrace what sets you apart, own your career and develop in ways you never expected. Leave your mark. And do it your way.

Our technology team is actively seeking an Insight Analyst to join its Applied Insights & Analytics team, helping transform data into actionable insights that drive better business decisions and commercial value. Working across areas including Trading, Buying & Merchandising, Supply Chain, Retail Operations, Finance, and Customer teams, the role involves analysing data, identifying opportunities, answering key business questions, and delivering clear, data-driven recommendations. As part of Primark’s innovative technology function, the successful candidate will collaborate with stakeholders and technology teams to support business growth, leveraging strong analytical skills and commercial awareness to turn complex data into meaningful outcomes.

 What You’ll Get 
 This role is a hybrid opportunity, offering 2-3 days Working from office.

People are at the heart of what we do here, so it’s essential we provide you with the right environment to perform at your very best.

Let’s talk lifestyle: Healthcare, pension and potential bonus. 27 days of leave, plus bank holidays and if you want, you can buy 5 more. Because Primark is all about tailoring to you, we offer Tax Saver Tickets, fitness centre and a subsidised cafeteria.  

 What You’ll Do as Insight Analyst 
 In your role, you’ll collaborate with different people across a range of skillsets. Here’s a flavour of your day-to-day:
 Deliver impactful business insights by partnering with stakeholders to understand commercial challenges, frame key business questions, and translate data into actionable recommendations that drive better decision-making.
 Analyse and interpret complex datasets using SQL, insight applications, and reporting tools to uncover trends, identify risks and opportunities, and support decisions across Trading, Customer, Retail Operations and other commercial functions.
 Create compelling data-driven stories by turning complex analytical outputs into clear, concise insights, visualisations, and recommendations that are easily understood by both technical and non-technical audiences.
 Develop and enhance reporting solutions, including dashboards, scorecards, and management reporting packs, ensuring outputs are accurate, consistent, user-friendly, and focused on delivering measurable business value.
 Drive continuous improvement by identifying manual processes, recurring business questions, and opportunities to streamline, standardise, and optimise reporting and insight delivery across the organisation.
 Collaborate with cross-functional Data & Analytics teams, including Business Partners, Senior Analysts, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists, while maintaining strong data quality standards and ensuring trusted, insight-led outcomes that support commercial growth and operational performance.
 

 What You’ll Bring   
 Here at Primark, we want everyone to feel valued – so please bring your authentic self to work, of course with some other key experience and abilities for this role in particular: 
 Experience in analytics, insights, reporting, or commercial analysis within retail, apparel, grocery, FMCG, or other fast-paced consumer-focused environments, with strong SQL skills and the ability to confidently query, analyse, and interpret data to support business decisions.
 Proficiency in Power BI, Tableau, or similar reporting and analytics tools, with experience creating insightful dashboards, scorecards, KPI frameworks, and performance reporting that drive measurable business outcomes.
 Strong commercial acumen with the ability to connect data and analysis to sales growth, conversion, margin improvement, markdown optimisation, stock availability, customer performance, and operational effectiveness.
 Excellent communication and data storytelling skills, with the ability to transform complex analytical findings into clear, compelling narratives, visualisations, recommendations, and decision-support materials for a wide range of stakeholders.
 Proven stakeholder management and commercial partnering experience, working collaboratively to understand business priorities, challenge assumptions constructively, shape analytical requirements, and deliver actionable insights linked to tangible value and benefits realisation.
 A proactive and solution-focused mindset, comfortable working with imperfect data, applying appropriate quality checks, improving reporting processes, simplifying decision-making, and identifying opportunities to enhance productivity, reporting efficiency, and overall business performance.
 

 Does this sound like you? Great, because we can’t wait to see what you’ll bring. You’ll be supported within a team of equally capable people, celebrating who you are and aiding you reach your potential. At Primark, we’re excited about our future - and we’re excited to develop yours.

 
 About Primark  
 At Primark, people matter. They’re the beating heart of our business and the reason we’ve grown from our first store in Dublin in 1969 to over 80,000 colleagues and over 480 stores in 18 countries today and growing. 
 So, what’s a career at Primark all about? The positive impact you’re making, the experiences you’re having and the people you’re with. It’s that feeling that turns a job into something more. Celebrating the wins, working at pace, and pulling through the challenging times with passion, courage, and your team by your side. It’s what drives us every day. 
 You’re our driving force. Embrace what sets you apart, own your career and develop in ways you never expected. Leave your mark. And do it your way. 
 

 #LI-Hybrid

Job Summary
Join our dynamic team as a Pharmacovigilance Analyst in the Pharma Research & Development sector. In this role, you will play a critical part in ensuring the safety and efficacy of pharmaceutical products through the monitoring, evaluation, and analysis of drug safety data. Working closely with cross-functional teams, regulatory authorities, and internal stakeholders, you will support pharmacovigilance activities and contribute to maintaining compliance with global regulatory requirements.
Responsibilities
Monitor and evaluate adverse event reports to ensure compliance with pharmacovigilance regulations and internal procedures.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyze, interpret, and communicate safety data effectively.
Prepare safety reports and support regulatory submissions in accordance with applicable guidelines and timelines.
Assist in the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of pharmacovigilance systems and processes.
Conduct literature reviews and surveillance activities to identify potential safety signals and emerging risks.
Support PV case processing activities while ensuring data quality, accuracy, and completeness.
Contribute to risk assessment and safety monitoring activities for pharmaceutical products.
Maintain accurate documentation and records to support audits, inspections, and regulatory compliance.
Participate in process improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness.
Stay current with pharmacovigilance regulations, industry trends, and best practices.
Qualifications
Degree in a relevant scientific discipline such as Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Medicine, Nursing, or a related field.
Experience in Pharma Research & Development.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex safety data.
Proficiency in pharmacovigilance data management and safety databases.
Excellent communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate across multiple stakeholders.
Experience in PV Case Processing.
Certification in Pharmacovigilance or Drug Safety Management is preferred.
Familiarity with risk management plans, safety assessments, and signal detection activities.
Up-to-date knowledge of pharmacovigilance regulations, guidelines, and industry standards.
Ability to mentor and support junior team members.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining high-quality standards.
Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Work Model
We believe hybrid work is the way forward as we strive to provide flexibility wherever possible. Based on this role's business requirements, this is a hybrid position requiring 2–3 days a week in a Cognizant office in Buenos Aires, Argentina . Regardless of your working arrangement, we are here to support a healthy work-life balance through our various wellbeing programs.

A career in one of the largest and fastest-growing IT services providers worldwide.
Ongoing support and funding with training and development plans.
Opportunity to work for leading global companies.
A diverse, collaborative, and inclusive work environment.

Certification in Pharmacovigilance or Drug Safety Management (preferred).

description:
Version 1 has celebrated 30 years in business and continues to be trusted by global brands to deliver technology and transformation solutions that drive customer success. Our deep expertise enables our customers to navigate the rapidly evolving technology landscape. We foster strong partnerships with global technology leaders including Microsoft, AWS, Oracle, Red Hat, OutSystems, Snowflake, ensuring that our customers are provided with the highest quality solutions and services. 
  We’re an award-winning employer reflecting how our employees are at the very heart of  what we do: 
 UK & Ireland's premier AWS, Microsoft & Oracle partner 
 3300+ strong, €350/£300m revenue business 
 10+ years as a Great Place to Work in Ireland & UK 
 Best Workplace for Women in the UK & Ireland by GPTW 
 Best Workplace for Wellbeing in the UK by GPTW 
 We’re a core values driven company, we hire people who share our values, and we reward those who display and foster them, it’s deeply embedded within our DNA. Invest in us and we’ll invest in you!. 

 We are seeking an experienced Lean Six Sigma / Business Process Optimisation Specialist to lead business process improvement initiatives within a large public-sector environment.
 The successful candidate will initially focus on functions and processes within the Data & Technology team , identifying and implementing measurable and sustainable improvements. Using Lean, Six Sigma and related methodologies, they will analyse existing processes, identify efficiencies, reduce variation and improve overall process quality.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Identify, quantify and prioritise business process improvement opportunities using data-driven analysis .
 Lead end-to-end business process optimisation and improvement initiatives .
 Apply Lean, Six Sigma and related process improvement methodologies to improve efficiency, reduce variation and enhance quality.
 Facilitate workshops with stakeholders across a range of business units and functions.
 Manage and engage stakeholders at all levels throughout business process change initiatives.
 Coach and mentor personnel in process improvement methodologies and practices.
 Work effectively with cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders .
 Communicate findings, recommendations and improvement opportunities in clear and practical language.
 

 Essential Requirements 
 Candidates must demonstrate:
 Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification from a recognised body.
 5+ years' experience leading and implementing process improvement initiatives within technology-led environments .
 A proven track record of delivering significant and quantifiable process efficiencies within a public-sector environment .
 Strong facilitation, coaching and presentation skills .
 Demonstrable experience working with cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders .
 

 Why Version 1?  
  At Version 1, we believe in providing our employees with a comprehensive benefits package that prioritises their wellbeing, professional growth, and financial stability. 
 Share in our success with our Quarterly Performance-Related Profit Share Scheme, where employees collectively benefit from a share of our company's profits 
 Strong Career Progression & mentorship coaching through our Strength in Balance & Leadership schemes with a dedicated quarterly Pathways Career Development programme 
 Flexible/remote working, Version 1 is tremendously understanding of life events and people’s individual circumstances and offer flexibility to help achieve a healthy work life balance 
 Financial Wellbeing initiatives including; Pension, Private Healthcare Cover, Life Assurance, Financial advice and an Employee Discount scheme 
 Employee Wellbeing schemes including Gym Discounts, Bike to Work, Fitness classes, Mindfulness Workshops, Employee Assistance Programme and much more. Generous holiday allowance, enhanced maternity/paternity leave, marriage/civil partnership leave and special leave policies 
 Educational assistance, incentivised certifications, and accreditations, including AWS, Microsoft, Oracle, and Red Hat 
 Reward schemes including Version 1’s Annual Excellence Awards & Star Awards. 
 Environment, Social and Community First initiatives allow you to get involved in local fundraising and development opportunities as part of fostering our diversity, inclusion and belonging schemes. 
 And many more exciting benefits… drop us a note to find out more.    
 Version 1 is an equal opportunities employer. 
 We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone feels valued and able to thrive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and lived experiences, and we value the different perspectives people bring including those shaped by disability and neurodiversity. 
 We want every candidate to have a positive and accessible recruitment experience. If you need reasonable adjustments at any stage of the process, please contact your recruiter ekta.bahl@version1.com at Version 1. We will consider all requests carefully, respectfully and confidentially.

title: Supply Chain Engineer (SCE)
description:
Job Details: 
 
 Job Description:  Supply Chain Engineer is responsible for driving improvement to factory manufacturing availability and to liaise with the factory on supplier labour issues (e.g. local FSE labour, supplier performance, long tool down recovery) for F25.
 
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Manage and drive quality issues related to supplier safety, quality, and site MQI closure performance. Scope may include chairing and leading 8D work with suppliers and modules to close prevention plans. Drive continuous improvement and quality improvement with supplier in partnership with partner FCS teams.

 Responsible for driving manufacturing availability (MA) performance across limiting toolsets within factory in partnership with modules. Includes problem definitions, roadmap building, and engagement/escalation with suppliers to resolve limiting module issues.

 Responsible to work with factory modules and factory leadership to improve cost structures, drive performance to outcome based contracts, and identify cost savings contracting opportunities across the functional areas within the local factory.

 As a senior SCE, the candidate is expected to lead/coach and mentor less experienced SCEs. They will be expected to drive VF wide improvements and standardization.

 
 
 Additional Responsibilities 
 
 Supports management/senior leadership to incorporate process and quality improvements in Intel's supply chain and logistics strategy. Defines material inspection methodology, conducts studies related to cost control, process control, and production yield, and implements plans and programs to optimize supply chain.

 Supports product long range plan development by defining next generation methodology capabilities to support Intel's supply chain roadmap. Explores and benchmarks emerging technology in the industry.

 Contributes to Intel's future technology definition and requirements. Highlights gaps between roadmap strategy, manufacturing capability, and market demands and recommends solutions to addresses those gaps.

 Tracks supply demand trends, conducts root cause analysis to find opportunities for process and quality improvements, and collaborates with supply chain leads to implement solutions.

title: Program Management Intern, Summer 2027 – Dublin, Ireland
description:
Our Purpose 
 
 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 
 
 Title and Summary 
 
Program Management Intern, Summer 2027 – Dublin, Ireland 
Why join Mastercard’s internship program? 

Mastercard's internship program offers more than hands-on work. It provides an opportunity to build skills, expand your network, and make a meaningful impact while working on projects that support business priorities. It provides an opportunity to build skills, expand your network, and make a meaningful impact while working on projects that support business priorities. 

We are hiring for two Program Management Intern openings, each supporting a different technology team. Please indicate clearly on your CV or cover letter which opportunity they are most interested in.

Technical Program Management:

Team profile

The Build Factory & Modernization team supports global data-centre and product deployments. The team coordinates technical delivery across engineering and partner teams, ensuring that dependencies are managed, progress is visible and the required components are ready for launch.

Role description

As a Technical Program Management Intern, you will support the planning, execution and delivery of a technical workstream from inception through completion. You will work across teams to coordinate engineering delivery, monitor dependencies and help address gaps or blockers that could affect successful delivery.

Your responsibilities may include:

Supporting the development and maintenance of integrated project schedules
Tracking data-centre deployments, product integrations, scope, timing and delivery
Coordinating work and dependencies across engineering and partner teams
Monitoring delivery progress and providing clear, data-supported updates
Identifying gaps, dependencies and blockers that may affect delivery
Supporting project delivery within established frameworks and processes
Reviewing metrics and identifying improved ways to provide program visibility
Developing knowledge in areas such as software engineering, data centres, security or operations
Turning complex or unstructured information into clear communications and instructions
Requirements

Requirements:

Availability: Must be available between 21st June until 27th August 2027
Undergraduate or master’s student with an expected graduation date between Dec 2027-July 2028

Currently studying:

Project Management or Program Management, Systems Analysis, Computing or Computer Science, Engineering or another relevant technical discipline

You should also have:

An interest in infrastructure, data-centre projects or new software-product deployments
An interest in supporting projects involving multiple stakeholders in a global organization
Strong technical aptitude and problem-solving skills
The ability to communicate complex infrastructure or technical information to non-technical and senior stakeholders
Clear and confident written and verbal communication skills
Curiosity and a willingness to build expertise in a technical domain
Availability to work onsite in the Dublin Tech Hub office at least three days per week

Program Management: 

Team profile

The Technology Regulatory Execution team supports the coordinated delivery of Mastercard’s technology regulatory obligations. The team works across functions to align priorities, dependencies and outcomes, while supporting effective governance, reporting and execution.

Role description

As a Program Management Intern, you will support program managers with the planning, execution and monitoring of strategic initiatives and projects. You will work with stakeholders across the organization to coordinate activities, track progress and help ensure that key deliverables are completed on time.

Your responsibilities may include:

Maintaining project schedules, milestones, action items and deliverables
Supporting leadership updates, presentations, dashboards and management reporting
Coordinating meetings, documenting decisions and following up on agreed actions
Monitoring program risks, issues and dependencies
Analyzing project and program data to identify actionable insights
Maintaining accurate documentation and governance records
Supporting process improvements that strengthen program efficiency and consistency
Learning how technology initiatives contribute to broader business and organizational priorities

Requirements

Availability: Must be available between 21st June until 27th August 2027
Undergraduate or master’s student with an expected graduation date between Dec 2027-July 2028

Currently studying: Project Management, Program Management, Business or a related discipline, with a demonstrated interest in technology, Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics, commonly referred to as 
Systems Analysis, Computing or Computer Science

You should also have:

An interest in supporting projects involving multiple stakeholders in a global organization
An interest in technology and how technology programs support business and regulatory objectives
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
The ability to understand technical topics and communicate them clearly to non-technical or senior stakeholders
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with different teams
Availability to work onsite in the Dublin Tech Hub office at least three days per week 
 
 Corporate Security Responsibility 
 
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

title: Futureforce Events & Admin Trainee
description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts. 
 
 Job Category 
Fixed Term & Temporary 
 Job Details 
 
 About Salesforce 
 Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
 
 Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
 
 
 
 About Salesforce & Future Pathways At Salesforce, we believe that talent is equally distributed, but opportunity is not. Our Future Pathways team is on a mission to change that, building pathways for the next generation of talent through world-class work experience programmes. Our participants in Dublin combine work and study over 18–36 months, gaining hands-on Salesforce experience while earning a recognized qualification.If you're passionate about people, programmes, and making things happen, we'd love to work with you.
 The Opportunity If you love the buzz of a well-run event, get satisfaction from a perfectly tracked catering order, and want to be part of something that genuinely changes lives — this could be the role for you.

We're looking for a motivated and organised trainee to join our Futureforce EMEA team in Dublin. Reporting to the Senior Manager for Programs & Events, Futureforce International, you'll be a key part of the operational engine that keeps our programmes and events running smoothly, from contracts and room bookings to catering, calendars, and community. This role is ideal for someone early in their career.

This is a hands-on, varied role where no two weeks look the same. You'll gain real experience across events, procurement, and programme coordination, all while being part of a global team of best-in-class events and programmes professionals, doing genuinely meaningful work for the next generation of talent. The length of the traineeship is twelve months.
 What You'll Be Working On Event Logistics & Execution You'll support the end-to-end delivery of Futureforce events in Dublin and across EMEA, from room booking and catering coordination, to on-site set-up and post-event wrap-up. You'll also help coordinate ad-hoc office tours and campus visits throughout the year.
 Community & Programme Support You'll help build and nurture the Futureforce community in Dublin, supporting intern cohort activities, coordinating community events, and helping create a welcoming, connected experience for participants throughout the year. This includes coordinating swag orders, communications, and other programme touchpoints.
 Contract & Procurement Administration You'll own the day-to-day administration of contracts and purchase orders (POs) for the team, raising and tracking POs, coordinating approvals, liaising with vendors, and ensuring everything is processed accurately and on time.
 Calendaring & Scheduling You'll manage team and programme calendars, coordinating scheduling across multiple stakeholders and ensuring the team always knows what's coming. You'll track key dates, send timely reminders, and keep logistical details organised and up to date.
 
 The Preferred Candidate Will Be highly organised with a strong attention to detail and a love of keeping things running smoothly
 Familiarity with AI tools, Tableau and comfortable using tools like Excel for tracking, reporting, and data management
 Have an interest in events, administration, or coordination (experience in a similar role is a plus but not required)
 Be a confident communicator, comfortable liaising with vendors, internal teams, and senior stakeholders alike
 Be comfortable with administrative processes such as PO management, contract tracking, and supplier coordination
 Be a self-starter who takes initiative and can juggle multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
 Eligible to participate in an accredited traineeship programme in Ireland
 
 Note: This role is office-flexible, and the expectation is to work from the office three days per week 
 
 
 
 
 Unleash Your Potential 
 When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and   be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can   do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world. 
 
 Accommodations 
 If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form . 
 
 Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options. 
 
 
 Posting Statement 
 Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.

title: Corporate Finance Associate 2027
description:
At Forvis Mazars, we’re not just one of the leading professional services firms in Ireland — we’re a launchpad for ambitious graduates ready to make an impact. With over 1,000 professionals across Dublin, Cork, Galway, and Limerick, and a global network spanning 100+ countries, we offer the scale, support, and opportunities to help you thrive.   
   
 Why join us?  
  
 Our next-generation graduate programme is built around you. We understand that no two people are the same, so we tailor your training, mentoring, and career development to match your strengths, interests, and goals.  
  
 Here, you’ll be more than just a number. You’ll be empowered to lead, innovate, and grow — personally and professionally. If you're looking for a career where your voice matters and your work makes a difference, this is the place for you. 
 
 The Position    
   
 Forvis Mazars Corporate Finance team advise clients on trade sales, private equity rounds, venture capital and management buy-outs. We have a wealth of experience on winning, executing and completing deals across a wide variety of sectors both nationally and internationally. 
  
 As a Forvis Mazars Associate, you will work side by side with Managers, Directors and Partners on all aspects of a transaction. You will learn financial modelling, how to prepare a business for sale, going to market, running an auction, running the due diligence process, coordinating legal due diligence, tax structuring the closing process and much more.
We’re looking for bright, motivated individuals from a wide range of backgrounds—whether that’s engineering, business, law, science, or a related field. We’ll equip you with the technical and business know-how you need—but your energy, curiosity, and attitude are what will set you apart.  
   
 What we’re looking for   
 You’re working towards or have recently completed an honours degree in any discipline.

 You value respect, inclusivity, and supporting those around you.

 You’re organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage your time effectively.  

 You’re comfortable with technology and have solid computer skills.  

 You think critically and enjoy solving problems with logic and creativity.  

 You have excellent organisational skills, computer literacy and attention to detail

Job Description: Data Operations, Investment Data Management
Role Overview
Location: Brazil
Function: Data Management
Working Hours: Aligned to the New York trading day, approximately 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM BRT, with a one-hour shift during U.S. daylight saving time. The role includes rotational coverage through New York end-of-day close and month-end cycles.
About the Role
The firm is an alternative asset manager focused on private credit, including direct lending, broadly syndicated and middle-market term loans, private placements, structured credit, opportunistic and special situations exposures. These investments are held across drawdown funds, evergreen vehicles, separately managed accounts, CLOs and rated feeder structures.
In this environment, data is core infrastructure. Every valuation, capital call, credit facility borrowing base, investor report, rating agency submission and regulatory filing depends on accurate security, fund, counterparty and pricing records.
This role sits at the front line of that infrastructure. The Data Operations Analyst / Senior Analyst will own golden-source master data domains, including Security Master, Fund Master, Counterparty Master and Pricing Master, and will partner closely with New York investment, trading and operations teams. The role requires managing a live operational function that opens the book each morning, absorbs intraday activity, resolves exceptions and closes the day cleanly before New York end-of-day.
Key Responsibilities
Master Data Ownership
Act as the golden-source owner for Security, Fund, Counterparty and Pricing master data across the private credit platform, ensuring accuracy, completeness, timeliness and consistency for all downstream consumers.
Define and enforce data standards, naming conventions, mandatory attribute sets and validation rules for each master data domain.
Maintain issuer and borrower corporate hierarchies, including relationships across legal entities, obligors, guarantors and ultimate parent entities, supported by research through public registries, filings and rating agency sources.
Data Quality and Controls
Design, run and continuously improve automated data quality checks, exception reports and tolerance-based alerting.
Operate within a “no surprises, no silent errors” control framework, ensuring every exception is logged, owned, aged and resolved to root cause.
Maintain maker-checker discipline, audit trails and supporting evidence sufficient for internal audit, external audit, SOC controls and regulatory review.
Operational Partnership
Serve as the Brazil-based partner to New York Trade Support, Middle Office, Portfolio Finance, Valuations, Treasury, Legal, Compliance and Investment teams.
Work directly with agent banks, custodians, fund administrators and data vendors to resolve discrepancies.
Escalate issues clearly, early and with context, including risk impact and proposed resolution.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Engineering, Information Systems or a related field.
3+ years of experience for Analyst level or 6+ years of experience for Senior Analyst level in investment operations, reference or master data management, middle office, back office, fund administration, loan operations or data governance at an asset manager, bank, administrator or financial data provider.
Working knowledge of at least one core asset class in scope, with corporate loans or term loans strongly preferred; experience with bonds, structured products, equities or OTC derivatives is also relevant.
Understanding of the instrument lifecycle, including setup, corporate actions, income and accruals, amendments, settlement and maturity or exit.
Strong Excel skills, including demonstrated ability to work with large data sets, reconcile across sources and investigate discrepancies independently.
Comfort operating on the New York clock, including end-of-day and month-end peak periods.

JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott Undergraduate Internship Programme 
 
 Unlock Your Potential at Abbott 
 Looking for an opportunity to apply your academic knowledge, gain hands-on experience, and make a real impact? Abbott's Undergraduate Internship Programme offers students the chance to work on meaningful projects, collaborate with industry experts, and contribute to innovations that help people live healthier lives.
 As an Abbott intern, you'll gain practical experience in a global healthcare organisation, develop sought-after skills, and build a strong professional network. Whether your interests lie in Engineering, Science, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, IT, or other STEM disciplines, you'll be supported to learn, grow, and reach your potential.
 Many of our interns go on to secure Graduate opportunities, Professional Development Programme positions, and long-term careers across Abbott's sites in Ireland and around the world.
 
 What You Can Expect 
 As an Abbott intern, you'll gain hands-on experience while working on meaningful projects that contribute to healthcare innovation. Depending on your area of study and placement, you may support engineering, manufacturing, scientific, quality, supply chain, business, or technology initiatives that make a real impact.
 
 What's in it for you? 
 Apply your academic learning in a real-world environment.
 Gain valuable hands-on experience with a global healthcare leader.
 Contribute to meaningful projects that help people live healthier lives.
 Learn from experienced professionals and receive ongoing mentorship.
 Develop technical, professional, and leadership capabilities.
 Build your network across Abbott's Ireland operations.
 Gain exposure to diverse functions, projects, and career paths.
 Benefit from 6, 9, or 12-month internship opportunities aligned to your academic programme.
 Explore future opportunities through Abbott's Graduate Programmes and long-term career pathways.
 Placement length and location will vary depending on business requirements and academic programme requirements. 
 
 About Abbott 
 Abbott is a global healthcare leader developing life-changing technologies that help people live healthier lives. With more than 122,000 colleagues serving people in over 160 countries, we deliver innovative solutions across diagnostics, medical devices, nutrition, and medicines.
 In Ireland, Abbott employs more than 6,200 people across ten sites, providing interns with the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in world-class STEM and business environments while contributing to healthcare innovation.
 Employment offers are subject to the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening. 
 
 Why Choose Abbott? 
 At Abbott, you'll gain hands-on experience, work on meaningful projects, and develop skills that will support your future career. You'll:
 Contribute to healthcare innovations that improve lives.
 Learn from experienced professionals and industry experts.
 Build valuable skills and expand your professional network.
 Gain exposure to opportunities across Abbott's Ireland network, with flexibility to be based at different Abbott locations.
 Explore future career opportunities within Abbott.
 Our internship Programme provides real-world experience, broad exposure, and a strong foundation for future career growth.
 
 Areas of Opportunity

 Specific assignments will be aligned to business requirements, site needs, and individual development opportunities 
 
 What You'll Bring 
 At Abbott, we're looking for students with the curiosity, drive, and ambition to make a difference. Successful candidates will:
 Be available for a 6, 9, or 12-month placement aligned with their academic programme.
 Be pursuing an undergraduate or postgraduate qualification in Supply Chain discipline 
 Be on track to achieve, or have achieved, a minimum 2.1 degree classificatio n.

 Demonstrate initiative, curiosity, and a desire to learn.
 Have a passion for innovation, STEM, and healthcare.

 Have flexibility to be based at any Abbott Ireland location, providing opportunities for broader exposure, diverse experiences, and professional growth.

Role: TPM – QA Tester (Issue Consolidation & Program Coordination)
Location & Workplace Requirement: Boulder (BLD) Office, On-site
Position Summary
We are seeking a detail-oriented Technical Program Manager (TPM) – QA Tester to support dogfood testing programs by driving issue consolidation, cross-functional coordination, reporting, and program execution. This role combines hands-on QA analysis with TPM responsibilities, ensuring user feedback and bug reports are effectively tracked, prioritized, communicated, and actioned across engineering and program teams.
Key Responsibilities
1. Issue Consolidation & Quality Validation
Review incoming dogfood bug reports, defects, and user feedback.
Analyze, categorize, and consolidate duplicate or related issues into actionable themes.

title: Plumbing Apprenticeship - Cork
description:
Join us, be part of more.   
   
 We’re so much more than an energy company. We’re a family of brands revolutionising how we power the planet. We're energisers. One team of 21,000 colleagues that's energising a greener, fairer future by creating an energy system that doesn’t rely on fossil fuels whilst living our powerful commitment to igniting positive change in our communities. Here, you can find more purpose, more passion, and more potential. That’s why working here is #MoreThanACareer. We do energy differently - we do it all. We make it, store it, move it, sell it, and mend it.   
   
 About your team:   
   
 We’re the pride of Ireland. Bord Gáis Energy have been powering the nation’s homes and businesses for almost 40 years. But now, we’re so much more than just gas and electric. Through our unique combination of household heroes and energy assets, we’re at the heart of the energy transition in Ireland, strengthening the country’s energy security and helping customers get ready for a net zero future.
 
 About Your Role 
 
 Step into a career where your curiosity, determination, and appetite for hands‑on learning really count. As a Plumbing Apprentice, you’ll play a vital role in helping households enjoy reliable, efficient heating - while building a future‑ready skillset you can be genuinely proud of.
 
 Whether you’re changing direction, starting fresh, or looking for a role with real purpose, this is your chance to grow. What matters most is your drive to learn, your problem‑solving spark, and your commitment to doing great work with care and confidence.
 Throughout your apprenticeship, you’ll combine practical workplace experience with mandatory off-the-job training. You’ll develop the skills, knowledge and practical experience needed to thrive. You'll develop the skills and experience needed to install, maintain and repair plumbing and heating systems - from everyday domestic work through to emerging technologies such as heat pumps, solar hot water systems, smart heating controls and full heating system installations. You’ll learn how to keep systems running safely and at their best, bringing older systems back to life and making smart upgrades that boost performance. With the support of experienced engineers, you’ll build the confidence, capability, and know-how to make a real difference from day one.
 
 This is a role where you'll make a real impact. You'll be out in the community, meeting customers, solving problems, and keeping homes safe and warm. No two days are the same - from fixing faults and maintaining plumbing and heating systems, to installing new technologies and helping customers run their systems more efficiently and reduce energy use. Every job is a chance to make a real difference.
 
 If you’re looking for a career with purpose, progression, and hands‑on learning - and you want to feel supported as you grow - this could be your next step. Bring your ambition. Bring your curiosity. We’ll help you turn it into a career that makes a difference. 
 
 Here's what we’re looking for:  
 
 You must be based in, or close to Cork

 Minimum of five passes at Leaving Certificate level, including Mathematics

 A valid full driving licence permitting the holder to drive in Ireland

 Ability to travel between customer and work locations as required

 Genuine interest in learning the plumbing trade and developing a long-term technical career

 Comfortable carrying out practical work and using hand and power tools

 Ability to work effectively as part of a team and learn from experienced engineers. 
 A willingness to take responsibility for your learning and successfully complete all workplace and off-the-job training and assessments. 
 Flexibility to attend mandatory off-the-job training at an assigned education or training location anywhere in Ireland. This may require travel and periods away from home 
 
 Here’s what's in it for you: 
 
 The opportunity to complete a nationally recognised Plumbing apprenticeship and become a qualified plumber. 

 Starting salary of €15,531 rising to €23,049 at 1 year, €34,573 at 2 years, & €41,487 after 3 years of your apprenticeship, with other add ons on top.

 Structured workplace learning and support from experienced engineers throughout your apprenticeship. 
 Practical experience across plumbing, heating systems and newer low-carbon technologies. 
 Opportunities to build your knowledge of heat pumps, smart heating controls and other technologies that support Ireland’s transition towards net zero. 
 Access to a range of Bord Gáis Energy and Centrica employee benefits. 
 As you near completion, you may have the opportunity to apply for a permanent Heating Engineer or Service Engineer role. Successful candidates will receive further training to support progression towards becoming a qualified Gas Engineer, with opportunities to develop additional skills in heat pumps and other low-carbon technologies that support our net zero ambitions. 
 
 Please note: We receive a high volume of applications for our apprenticeship opportunities and may close this advert early if enough applications are received. To avoid missing out, we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible.
 
 Bord Gáis Energy is committed to placing equality, diversity, care and respect at the heart of our policies and everyday practices. We encourage everyone to take part in our active employee networks, including the Women’s Network, REACH, the Neurodiversity Network and BRÓD. Our vision is to employ a diverse mix of people who reflect the communities we work in and the customers we serve. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds and perspectives.
 
 Why should you apply?    
  
We’re not a perfect place – but we’re a people place. Our priority is supporting all of the different realities our people face. Life is about so much more than work. We get it. That’s why we’ve designed our total rewards to give you the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, making sure that you and your family are supported not only financially, but physically and emotionally too. Visit the link below to discover why we’re a great place to work and what being part of more means for you.  
  
 https://www.morethanacareer.energy/bordgais  
   
 If you're full of energy, fired up about sustainability, and ready to craft not only a better tomorrow, but a better you, then come and find your purpose in a team where your voice matters, your growth is non-negotiable, and your ambitions are our priority.    
 
 Help us, help you. We would love for you to share any information about yourself throughout our recruitment process so that we can better understand you and help shape your journey.

We are looking for an experienced Grafana L3 Engineer/Administrator to manage and support enterprise Grafana environments. title: IT Service Desk Analyst
description: Deloitte is the biggest professional services Firm in the world and making an impact is more than just what we do: it’s why we’re here. We’re driven to create positive progress for our clients, community, people, and the planet. This sense of purpose inspires us to work to the highest standards, to tackle the challenges that matter. We offer a competitive starting salary of €32,500.00 for this role, with salary adjustments reflecting your experience level and expertise. . Why you'll enjoy this new opportunity Join Deloitte's IT Service Desk team and become the critical first point of contact for our organisation's technology needs. This role sits at the heart of our operations, directly impacting how effectively our teams work and serve our clients. You'll own the end-to-end resolution of technical issues, from initial diagnosis through deployment, while building strong relationships across the business. If you thrive on solving problems, supporting colleagues, and making a tangible difference in how technology enables our people, this is your opportunity to grow into a trusted technical leader. Key skills and prior experience that align well with this position Technical troubleshooting expertise: Proven ability to diagnose and resolve hardware, software, and network issues across multiple platforms and systems Client service orientation: Strong communication and relationship-building skills with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users Organisational and administrative capability: Excellent prioritisation, multi-tasking, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage competing demands in a fast-paced environment IT foundation knowledge: Qualification or demonstrated experience in Computer Science, Business Computing, or equivalent technical background; motivation to build a sustained career in IT What type of work will I be doing? Provide first and second level technical support to end users, diagnosing and resolving hardware, software, and network issues through systematic troubleshooting and research Log, track, and manage all incidents and service requests, ensuring timely updates and resolution within agreed service levels Deploy new hardware, software, and peripheral equipment to end users, ensuring proper configuration and user enablement Assist with the scheduling, coordination, and delivery of the hardware refresh program across the organisation Support the wider IT team with escalations, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving on complex issues Provide administrative assistance to the IT Management Team, including documentation, reporting, and process support Contribute to continuous improvement of service desk processes and user experience through feedback and suggestions Who is the Hiring Manager? The hiring manager is an experienced IT Service Delivery leader within Deloitte, recognised for their collaborative and supportive approach to team management. They prioritise open communication, professional development, and creating a positive, inclusive team environment where technical excellence and user satisfaction go hand in hand. Where is this role based? This role is based in Dublin and requires being onsite 5 days per week If you believe that you meet most of the criteria above, we encourage you to apply. Deloitte is an equal opportunities employer and will ensure any reasonable accommodations are implemented as part of the recruitment and selection process. What we offer Your reward at Deloitte is competitive, supports our purpose and enables our people to never stop growing. Your reward at Deloitte is not just your salary, we believe in investing in our people's personal and professional development and empowering their work-life balance. Our ambition is to achieve gender equality and enable continuous growth. We offer supports and benefits that suit you, wherever you are in life, including health and well-being, pension, savings, training, coaching and enhanced leave options among others. Keep on being you. Bring your full, absolute self to work, every day. Explore, question and collaborate. Stretch your thinking, while building a career that inspires and energises you. And, whatever motivates you, keep growing both professionally and personally – because when you make an impact that matters, we do too. Deloitte is the number one professional services firm in the world, and the leading global provider of audit and assurance, consulting, financial advisory, risk advisory, sustainability, tax, and related services. We have offices across Ireland in Dublin, Belfast, Cork, Limerick and Galway. Deloitte is proud of the enhanced flexibility that we offer our people through our hybrid working strategy, Deloitte Works. It means we trust our people with the flexibility and control to make the right choices in where, when, and how they work. Deloitte is looking for people that have a leadership mindset, are curious, enjoy solving challenges and are eager to grow their careers.
