Who we are looking for: 
 Based in the Dublin office, you will be part of a team of 200+ dedicated financial reporting professionals who are focused on delivering interim and annual US GAAP/IFRS financial statements to a diverse group of alternative investment managers. 
 
 Why this role is important to us: 
 The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Global Services (SSGS). SSGS gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping, to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGS’ tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.
 Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
 
 What you will be responsible for: 
 As a Financial Reporting Officer you will
 Plan, schedule, and manage the production of interim / annual financial statements and daily workflow for multiple alternative investment client relationships and product types (hedge, private equity, and real estate funds).
 Act as the primary point of contact for clients with responsibility for implementing and supporting the service requirements of the various client relationships serviced within the group.

 Perform technical reviews of hedge, private equity, and real estate funds’ financial statements in accordance with relevant GAAP and regulatory requirements.

 Set individual and team targets and priorities; maintain high standards of client service; conduct performance appraisals and give feedback on individual and team performance.

 Be a source of technical support and guidance, including reviewing financial statements prepared by your teams and ensuring that all financial statements are accurate and prepared in accordance with the relevant GAAP prior to issuance to external parties (clients / auditors).

 Support new business integration and ensure operating models are designed to deliver best of breed service to clients leveraging global footprint as necessary.

 Manage your own continued professional development, through engaging in the performance review process and attending relevant training as per agreed training curriculum.

 Deputise for your assistant vice president as required from time to time.

 Perform other duties as required from time to time.

 
 What we value 
 These skills will help you succeed in this role
 Excellent communicate skills

 Strong leadership abilities.

 Excellent attention to detail

 Strong knowledge of accounting standards as they relate to funds (IFRS, Irish GAAP in particular)

 Ability to multi-task and be comfortable with managing difficult situations as they arise. 

 Be able to communicate effectively with colleagues, clients, auditors at all levels.

 Experience of working to deadlines.

 Ability to delegate work to others.

 Ability to effectively represent the team to clients and internal stakeholders

 
 Education & Preferred Qualifications 
 Possess a degree in finance, business / accounting or related discipline,

 Have 6-8 years’ experience working in a similar environment or related environment, including experience managing staff

 The role would also suit someone who is a qualified professional accountant (eg. ACA, ACCA, CPA).

 The candidate should possess strong knowledge of US GAAP/IFRS investment company financial statements with previous experience servicing alternative investments..

 
 Disposition 
 Self-motivated

 Good initiative

 Professional

 Multi-tasking ability

 Enthusiastic

 Adaptable – ability to develop new approaches to solving problems

 Flexible

 Strong inter-personal skills

For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. title: Bioprocess Associate - Drug Substance
description:
Job Description
 
 An exciting opportunity a Bioprocess Associate (Drug Substance) has arisen  at our Dundalk manufacturing facility, you will be a key member of our fast-growing, dynamic startup, working with cutting-edge technology. 

 This role is focused on delivering to the patient through living the Dundalk culture, including a commitment to safety, focusing on right first time in everything we do, and concentrating on the engagement and development of self and peers.

 The role is currently on Days but will transition to 4 cycle 12/7.

 Bring energy, knowledge, innovation to carry out the following: 
 Manufacture drug substance through inoculation, cell expansion, and bioreactor activities, leading to filtration and purification of the product in a state-of-the-art single-use technology-based facility.
 Set up single-use equipment between runs and carry out the production process according to world-class GMP and EHS principles.
 Perform manufacturing processes including DS Downstream Processing (DSP), Upstream Processing (USP), and Buffer/Media preparation.
 Carry out all production operations in the assigned area as per the relevant SOPs and Manufacturing Batch Records.
 Assist in maintaining a safety-oriented, cGMP-compliant work environment at all times.
 Write, review, and revise area Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), On the Job Training (OJT’s), Production Batch Records (PBRs), Logbooks, Training Competencies, and Work Instructions.
 Train and mentor colleagues in SOPs, process execution, and equipment operation.
 Support the Manufacturing team to consistently deliver on specific area Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), e.g., Safety, Quality, Schedule adherence, Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), and team training.
 Assist with the investigation of and operations deviations through the Quality System, engaging with all relevant personnel and functions as appropriate.
 Lead and actively participate in shift handovers.
 Liaise with the Shift Lead regarding issues that may arise within the production area, including highlighting operational challenges.
 Use Lean Tools as part of daily operations (Standard Work, 5S, TPM, Gemba, Method 1, our company Production System (MPS)) to optimize efficiency and drive the culture of Continuous Improvement (CI).
 Provide assistance and/or support maintenance, engineering, quality, or other colleagues as requested.
 Conduct all activities in accordance with Company policies & SOPs & global regulatory guidelines (including cGMP/cGLP/cGCP), environmental guidelines, as appropriate.
 Support the development, commissioning & qualification of new vaccines drug substance manufacturing equipment and subsequent transition to commercial manufacturing.
 

 What skills you will need: 
 Certificate, Diploma, Degree, Trade qualification, or equivalent demonstrated experience of 12 months or more in a regulated environment, GMP environment.
 Knowledge and experience of relevant cGMP, safety, and environmental regulations within the biopharmaceutical industry.
 Experience with recording information in real-time using electronic or manual systems.
 Experience in executing operations while following SOPs, Batch Records, and Manufacturing Controls Systems.
 Experience in the biopharmaceutical industry.
 Experience of working in Grade C, D, and CNC environments.
 
 Ireland – The Company: 
 Within our Company in Ireland, we work at the forefront of science and technology to advance manufacturing excellence and R&D across our Irish sites and global company network. We’re always looking to make a difference for people, patients, and communities – from our Company in Ireland to the world.

 Our Commitment to Ireland: 

 Ireland is one of the Ireland’s leading healthcare companies, having first established here over 50 years ago. We have a dynamic and team of over 3,000 employees currently working across seven sites in Ballydine, Co Tipperary, Brinny, Co Cork, Dunboyne, Co Meath, Carlow, and Dublin, where, in addition, operate substantial Human Health and Animal Health businesses. Through our long-standing footprint in Ireland and over $6 billion invested across our Irish operations, our Irish sites manufacture many of our Company’s top products, helping save and enhance lives in over 140 countries around the world.

 As a cutting-edge, state-of-the-art vaccines facility spanning over 15,500 square metres across three stories, our Dundalk site will focus on qualification, continued product development and expanding its capabilities within our network. Featuring drug substance manufacturing, drug product manufacturing and quality control labs that will support the global supply of vaccine products - strengthening our ability to make an impact on people and patients worldwide by adding new capabilities to our already industry-leading network

Join us to put AI to work for people.
Job Description
About the Role:
We are seeking strategic, curious and driven  Finance Interns  to join our  Finance Intern Program.  Interns will be placed within a specific finance function through a matching process. In your placement, you’ll contribute to meaningful projects and gain valuable, hands-on experience in a  12-week long summer internship .
We are seeking students with an  AI first mindset  —those eager to think differently, challenge the status quo, and help shape the future of finance. As Customer Zero, our finance team plays a critical role in advancing ServiceNow’s company priorities: leading in AI innovation, driving scalable growth, and delivering operational excellence. This is an exciting opportunity to build foundational finance skills while contributing innovative thinking to a rapidly evolving business landscape
High-performing interns that are graduating the next summer may be considered for full-time opportunities through our Finance Development Rotation Program (FDRP), a post-graduate program designed to accelerate careers through structured rotations, mentorship, and exposure to finance leadership.
Opportunities are available across multiple teams and may include:
Financial Planning & Analysis
Corporate Accounting & Financial Services
Go-To-Market Finance
Treasury
Strategic Finance
What you’ll do:
Contribute to high-impact projects that support financial decision-making across the business
Analyze financial data, build models , and prepare insights that influence budgets, forecasts, and strategic plans
Support month-end and quarter-close processes, reporting, and variance analysis
Partner cross-functionally with teams across the business
Participate in intern programming, development workshops, and networking events
Qualifications
Who you are:
Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.
Able to commit to a 12-week summer internship at our headquarters in West Palm Beach, Fl
Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field with a December 2027 or later graduation date
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Experience with finance and accounting concepts through coursework or prior work/internship experience
Demonstrated curiosity and interest in AI, with a passion for exploring how artificial intelligence can improve finance processes and decision-making
Experience using AI tools and automated workflows is a plus
Self-starter with strong initiative, attention to detail, and excellent organizational skills
Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint)
Why work with us:
Join a finance team that is a pioneer in applying AI to transform finance workflows and decision-making
Work on meaningful projects that directly impact business outcomes while building foundational finance skills
Experience a supportive and collaborative environment that encourages curiosity, innovation, and growth
Participate in development workshops, networking events, and mentorship programs designed to accelerate your learning
Be part of a fast-growing SaaS company where your work contributes to scalable growth and operational excellence

description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott in Ireland 
 Abbott has maintained a strong presence in Ireland since 1946 and celebrates its 80th anniversary in the country in 2026. The company supports the Irish healthcare sector with a broad portfolio spanning diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. Today, Abbott employs more than 6,200 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.
 
 About Abbott 
 Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.
 
 Abbott Ireland Diagnostic Division Sligo  
 Abbott Diagnostic's is a global leader of in vitro diagnostics with approximately 70,000 institutional customers in more than 100 countries. Our diagnostic products offer a broad range of innovative instrument systems and tests for hospitals, reference labs, blood banks, physician offices and clinics. 
 Abbott’s diagnostic products offer customers automation, convenience, cost effectiveness and flexibility. Abbott has helped transform the practice of medical diagnosis from an art to a science, helping to create the modern diagnostics industry through the company's commitment to improving patient care and lowering overall costs. The history of Abbott Diagnostics is filled with examples of first-of-a-kind products and significant technological advancements. 
 
 *Please note any offer of employment for this position is conditional upon the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical practitioner designated by the Company.”
 
 About the Role 
 We are seeking a highly motivated and analytical Accountant to join our Finance team. This role will support the site's financial planning, forecasting, reporting, and business performance analysis activities while also serving as the Site Customs Coordinator, ensuring compliance with customs regulations and trade requirements.
 The successful candidate will work closely with Finance, Supply Chain Procurement and Logistics, and external customs authorities to provide actionable financial insights and maintain robust customs compliance processes.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 
 Financial Planning & Analysis 
 Support the annual budgeting, quarterly forecasting, and long-range planning processes.

 Prepare monthly financial performance reports and variance analysis against budget and forecasts.

 Develop and maintain financial models to support decision-making and business performance improvement initiatives.

 Analyse manufacturing costs, inventory performance, and operational KPIs.

 Partner with functional leaders to identify risks, opportunities, and cost improvement initiatives.

 Support month-end and year-end close activities, reporting, and financial analysis.

 Prepare presentations and management reports for site leadership.

 Drive continuous improvement in reporting processes, data analytics, and dashboard development.

 
 Customs & Trade Compliance 
 Act as the site's Customs Coordinator and subject matter expert for customs compliance.

 Ensure compliance with all relevant customs regulations, import/export requirements, and internal policies.

 Maintain customs documentation and records in accordance with regulatory requirements.

 Coordinate customs audits and support interactions with customs authorities and external brokers.

 Review and monitor tariff classifications, country of origin determinations, and customs valuation requirements.

 Partner with Supply Chain, Logistics, Procurement, and external service providers to resolve customs-related issues.

 Monitor changes in customs legislation and assess potential business impacts.

 Support implementation and maintenance of customs compliance procedures and training.

 Identify opportunities to optimise customs processes, duty management, and trade compliance controls.

 
 Qualifications and Skills 
 
 Required 
 Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, Business, or related discipline.

 Professional accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CPA) or finalist level.

 3+ years' experience in accounting, financial analysis, or FP&A within a manufacturing environment.

 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

 Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

 Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

 Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.

 Preferred 
 Experience in customs, import/export compliance, or international trade operations.

 Experience working with ERP systems (e.g., SAP).

 Knowledge of customs regulations and duty management processes.

 Experience with Power BI, data analytics, or reporting tools.

 Experience working in a regulated manufacturing environment.

 Key Competencies 
 Financial analysis and business partnering

 Attention to detail and accuracy

 Regulatory compliance mindset

 Process improvement orientation

 Effective communication and influencing skills

 Cross-functional collaboration

 Continuous learning and adaptability

 What Success Looks Like 
 Delivery of accurate and insightful financial planning and reporting.

 Strong partnership with operational and functional leaders.

 Maintenance of a compliant customs environment with successful audit outcomes.

 Identification of opportunities that improve business performance and process efficiency.

 Effective management of customs risks while supporting uninterrupted supply chain operations.

 
 Learn more about our health and wellness benefits, which provide the security to help you and your family live full lives:  Abbott in Ireland | Benefits 
 
 Connect with us at www.abbott.com and on LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram , X and YouTube .

JOB DESCRIPTION: About Abbott 
 Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 114,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.
 
 Abbott in Ireland 
 Abbott has been operating in Ireland since 1946 and serves the Irish market with a diverse range of healthcare products including diagnostics, diabetes care, medical devices and nutritional products. In Ireland, Abbott currently employs about 6,000 people across ten sites located in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford and Sligo.
 Please note any offer of employment for this position is conditional upon the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical
 practitioner designated by the Company
 
 Abbott Diabetes Care Kilkenny 
 Abbott Diabetes Care has opened  a new site, in Kilkenny, that is  at the forefront of Diabetes care with the latest technology, to manufacture FreeStyle blood glucose test strips and FreeStyle Sensors for use in diabetes management. Among Abbott Diabetes Care leading brands are the FreeStyle Precision, FreeStyle Lite and FreeStyle Libre systems.
 
 About the Role This role plays a critical part in ensuring compliance, product quality, and operational excellence within a regulated manufacturing environment. The Validation Engineer will lead qualification activities for sustaining projects while collaborating with cross-functional teams to support new product introductions and process improvements. The position will focus on Process Validation, Equipment Qualification, and associated validation activities to ensure manufacturing processes remain compliant, efficient, and capable of delivering high-quality products.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Lead Process Validation and Equipment Qualification activities for sustaining projects.

 Develop and implement validation strategies for new product introductions in collaboration with R&D, Quality Assurance, PMO, and Global Engineering teams.

 Complete impact assessments for proposed process changes and new products to determine validation requirements.

 Generate, execute, review, and approve validation protocols and validation reports.

 Support Process and Software Validation activities across the manufacturing site.

 Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing processes and software systems.

 Support the implementation and validation of process improvements.

 Drive compliance and operational excellence through effective validation practices.

 Manage multiple projects and priorities while adhering to established timelines.

 Communicate project progress and validation status updates to management and key stakeholders.

 Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to ensure successful project delivery.

 Provide guidance and mentoring to junior engineering team members.

 Ensure compliance with corporate policies, divisional procedures, and regulatory requirements.

 Maintain a strong understanding of current cGMP requirements and industry regulations.

 Education & Experience: NFQ Level 7 qualification (or equivalent) in Engineering, Science, Manufacturing, or a related technical discipline.

 Minimum of 2 years' relevant industry experience.

 Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment is preferred.

 Experience within high-volume manufacturing operations would be advantageous.

 Knowledge of validation methodologies, qualification activities, and cGMP requirements.

 
 What we Offer 
 Attractive compensation package that includes competitive pay, as well as benefits such as
 Family health insurance,

 Excellent pension scheme

 Life assurance

 Career Development

 Fantastic new facility

 Growing business plus access to many more benefits.

 
 Connect with us at www.abbott.com or https://www.ie.abbott/, on LinkedIn at www.linkedin.com/company/abbott-/, on Facebook at www.facebook.com/Abbott and on Twitter @AbbottNews.

At AIB, our values guide how we work and how we support each other. You’ll treat colleagues and customers with fairness and Show Respect , and you’ll thrive in a culture built on collaboration where we Be One Team to deliver meaningful impact.
Location/Office Policy:   This role is Hybrid - 3 days in the office (currently 2 days Molesworth Street and 1 day in Central Park)
Do you want to play a leading role in the global fight against financial crime?
Do you want a role that is challenging, rewarding and all about keeping AIB and its customers safe from the harm of financial crime?
Are you ready to work in a team of AML/CFT experts, guiding and challenging the business to make sure the Bank meets all its legal and regulatory obligations around money‑laundering, terrorist financing and wider financial crime risks?
What is the Role:
The AML/CFT Compliance Team is part of the Financial Crime Unit, and is a 2nd Line of Defence function.
The team provides Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) advice, guidance and support to the business and their business governance teams in relation to the practical application of money laundering and terrorist financing regulations.
The role holder will provide co-ordinated second line oversight, challenge, and advisory support to ensure AIB meets its statutory and regulatory obligations across AML and CFT risk management.
The role holder plays a key part in embedding the Group Financial Crime Framework, driving high standards of regulatory compliance, strengthening risk culture, and supporting strategic transformation initiatives.
Key accountabilities :
In line with the Bank’s three lines of defence model, support the Team’s senior management in the implementation of the Bank’s AML/CFT Framework (Policy, Standards, Procedures).
Support the team’s senior management with the Bank’s planning and implementation of various AML/ CFT projects and initiatives.
Monitor emerging AML/CFT risks, legal/regulatory developments, industry guidance, and assessing applicability to the Bank.
Positively influence and challenge businesses areas to ensure that adequate and effective AML/CFT Controls are implemented and maintained.
Identify and analyse AML/ CFT issues and concerns to determine emerging trends, provide M.I. to senior management and provide input into bespoke training material programmes written for business teams
Oversee the management of the Group AML/CFT Compliance mailbox and provide day to day support to the business and their business governance teams in relation to AML/ CFT queries
What you Will Bring;
Previous experience within a Compliance or Control function
Understanding of current and emerging Financial Crime risks across the banking and financial services industry
Previous experience in interpretation of legislation and/or knowledge of AML/CFT regulation
Strong planning and organisational skills with an ability to work to tight deadlines
Strong verbal and written communication skills

title: Risk and Compliance Analyst
description:
The Apex Group was established in Bermuda in 2003 and is now one of the world’s largest fund administration and middle office solutions providers.
 
 Our business is unique in its ability to reach globally, service locally and provide cross-jurisdictional services. With our clients at the heart of everything we do, our hard-working team has successfully delivered on an unprecedented growth and transformation journey, and we are now represented by over circa 13,000 employees across 112 offices worldwide.Your career with us should reflect your energy and passion.
 
 That’s why, at Apex Group, we will do more than simply ‘empower’ you. We will work to supercharge your unique skills and experience.
 
 Take the lead and we’ll give you the support you need to be at the top of your game. And we offer you the freedom to be a positive disrupter and turn big ideas into bold, industry-changing realities.
 
 For our business, for clients, and for you
 
 
 Risk and Compliance Analyst   
 About FundRock Management Company (Ireland) Limited 
   
 FundRock Management Company (Ireland) Limited (‘FMCIL’) is a third party UCITS Fund Management Company & Alternative Investment Fund Manager authorised and regulated by the Central Bank of Ireland with assets under management of approx. €100 Billion.
  
 Our clients’ funds range from under €100m AUM to over €10bn with a diverse set of strategies and investment security types.
  
 FMCIL’s objective is to protect shareholders' interests by helping clients to comply with their regulatory requirements. We pride ourselves on delivering first-class client service through a motivated team. Our Irish operations consist of approximately 75 people from fund administration, investment management, legal, compliance and risk backgrounds.
  
   
 About Apex Group 
  
 FMCIL is part of the Apex Group. Apex, established in Bermuda in 2003, is a global financial services provider which has more than $3 trillion of assets under administration. With over 94 offices worldwide and over 12,000 employees, Apex delivers an extensive range of services to asset managers, capital markets and family offices. The Apex Group supports Asset Managers through three key lines of service: Fund Solutions, Financial Solutions and Corporate Solutions.
   
   
 The Opportunity 
  
 The successful candidate will report to the Designated Person for Fund Risk and support the Risk function in providing independent oversight and challenge across investment compliance, regulatory reporting and valuation risk.
  
 The role involves regular engagement with senior management, internal teams and external stakeholders to identify, investigate and resolve risk issues. It presents a unique opportunity to contribute directly to the governance and performance of a dynamic Fund Management Company.
   
 The position – key responsibilities: 
   
 1. Investment Compliance Oversight 

 Perform ongoing investment compliance monitoring across funds under management (UCITS and AIFs). Review investment compliance exception/breach reports, investigate potential breaches and assess their nature, materiality and impact.
 Liaise with external stakeholders (Investment Managers, Administrators and Depositaries) regarding potential and confirmed breaches, assess/challenge proposed remediation and monitor corrective actions through to completion.
 Support periodic reviews of investment restrictions and compliance monitoring arrangements.
 Escalate material or recurring breaches in accordance with the risk and governance framework.
 Assist in the implementation of the internal Fund Risk Management framework as part of new product initiatives and fund launches.
 Assist the Fund Risk team in the preparation of both regular and exception-based risk reporting for both fund boards and the management company that enables each to fulfil their governance obligations related to the risk management of investment funds under their management.
 
 2. Regulatory Reporting 

 Support the preparation, review and oversight of regulatory reporting obligations applicable to the funds under management and the management company.
 Review regulatory returns and supporting information for completeness, consistency and reasonableness.
 Investigate discrepancies and ensure appropriate remediation
 Monitor the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of regulatory submissions.
   
 Experience required: 
   
 1+ years’ relevant experience in the UCITS and/or EU Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) frameworks.
 Relevant finance or quantitative degree, with certification or progress towards qualifications such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or CAIA.
 An understanding of the AIFM and UCITS regulatory frameworks, particularly in relation to risk management requirements.
 Excellent communication and reporting skills, with the ability to interpret complex financial data and convey insights effectively to stakeholders, including portfolio managers, fund directors, and senior management.
 Energetic and solutions-driven team player, willing to support and collaborate with colleagues.
 Self-starter with a detail-oriented and pragmatic approach to problem-solving.
 Adaptable, creative, and capable of addressing diverse client needs effectively
 
 Disclaimer : Unsolicited CVs sent to Apex (Talent Acquisition Team or Hiring Managers) by recruitment agencies will not be accepted for this position. Apex operates a direct sourcing model and where agency assistance is required, the Talent Acquisition team will engage directly with our exclusive recruitment partners.

title: Payroll Specialist 1 year contract
description:
Payroll Specialist (1 year contract) 
 Ireland/UK 
 Full-time 
 Hybrid 
 About the Role 
 We’re looking for a detail-oriented Payroll Specialist to enable end-to-end payroll operations across EMEA. You will manage multi-country payroll cycles, ensure statutory compliance, partner with in-country providers (ICPs), and deliver accurate and timely payrolls for a diverse employee population. Experience with ADP Celergo (preferred) and core HRIS/payroll integrations like Oracle HCM is essential. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, global environment and brings a strong control mindset with excellent stakeholder management.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 End-to-End Payroll Processing

 Prepare, validate, and process monthly/fortnightly payrolls across multiple EMEA countries.

 Own gross-to-net calculations, off-cycles, retros, and reconciliations.

 Review pre- and post-payroll reports, audit files, GL postings, and variance analyses.

 Compliance & Controls

 Ensure statutory compliance with local country tax, social security, pensions, and benefit-in-kind requirements.

 Maintain robust controls, documentation, and audit readiness (internal & external).

 Coordinate year-end activities and complete on time to support employees for filing returns

 Vendor & ICP Management

 Partner with ADP Celergo (and/or other ICPs) for country-specific processing, SLAs, and issue resolution.

 Monitor vendor performance, drive root-cause analysis, and continuous improvements.

 HRIS & Integrations

 Validate and reconcile Oracle HCM/inbound/outbound payroll interfaces (new hires, terms, transfers, comp changes).

 Employee Support & Case Management

 Manage payroll queries and responding via the helpdesk/case management tool (e.g., ServiceNow,  Freshservice).

 Accounting & Finance Partnership

 Reconcile payroll accounts, support journal entries, and month-end close (accruals, provisions).

 Support treasury with funding files, bank payments, net pay, and statutory remittances.

 Operational Excellence

 Maintain and enhance SOPs, process maps, and control checklists.

 Lead/participate in projects: country transitions, M&A integrations, system enhancements, and new market entries.

 Track KPIs and drive continuous improvement (quality, timeliness, cost, and employee experience).
 

 Required Qualifications & Experience 
 6–8 years of progressive payroll experience, with multi-country exposure in   EMEA.

 Strong command of payroll processing and statutory compliance across APAC and EMEA countries.

 Hands-on experience working with ADP Celergo, ADP Vantage and ADP Streamline will be added advantage

 Proficient with Oracle HCM payroll integrations and data validation.

 Experience using a helpdesk/case tool (e.g., ServiceNow) for payroll tickets and SLAs.

 Good understanding of GL mapping, payroll accounting, and bank/payment files.

 Advanced Excel (lookups, pivots, reconciliations); strong data accuracy and numerical reasoning.

 Excellent communication and stakeholder management across time zones.

 Country-specific expertise (e.g., Belgium, Lux, Switzerland, Netherland and Nordic countries. 

 Knowledge of benefits in payroll, shadow payroll, and mobility/expat cases.

  
 Core Skills & Competencies 
 Technical: payroll calculations, statutory filings/remittances, year-end reporting, GL & reconciliations, interface validations.

 Compliance: country payroll laws, social security, pensions/super, tax deadlines, reporting formats.

 Systems: ADP Celergo (preferred), Oracle HCM, Workday, helpdesk tools

 Behavioural: ownership, integrity, attention to detail, problem-solving, discretion with sensitive data, collaboration.
 

 Education & Certifications 
 Bachelor’s degree or master’s in accounting/finance/HR or related field (or equivalent experience).
 

 Work Schedule 
 Ability to support cross-regional time zones during payroll cycles and critical cut-offs.

title: Operations & Logistics Internship, Amazon Logistics
description:
Amazon Operations is the backbone of the Amazon customer experience. With over 50 fulfilment centres, hundreds of delivery stations, and tens of thousands of employees, the team works together to efficiently deliver items to customers. In the fulfilment centres, millions of items are picked and packed annually, while delivery teams work to get orders to customers on time. description:
About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 About the Role 
 
 The role is based in our Limerick office and will be within our Fund Administration Division where you will be part of a flexible and collaborative work culture.
 This role will provide the partner with an opportunity to develop both knowledge and experience of a dynamic environment in which they will assist the team with producing and providing oversight on a wide variety of regulatory solutions for submission across Europe.
 We have a balanced hybrid working model to ensure you get the flexibility you need, and the successful candidate will spend their time between working in the office and working from home.
 
 The key responsibilities of the role include: 
 Assist the team on the provision of daily and periodic regulatory reporting solutions

 Engage with Northern Trust clients, internal departments, Regulators and Relationship Management on any queries on our existing reporting solutions or on adhoc information requests.

 Assist Business Analysts with the building of solutions to fulfil new reporting obligations.

 Assist with responding to queries on Regulatory Reporting requirements.

 Participate in the cross training of partners across EMEA and outsourced locations.

 Promote a proactive and constructive relationship with the team partners based in Manila which provides support on the regulatory solutions.

 Assisting with the development of operational efficiencies and process improvements to increase customer satisfaction.

 
 Relationships and Stakeholders 
 Direct Manager – Regulatory Reporting Section Manager

 Internal Stakeholders – Fund Administration Leaders, New Business Teams, Relationship Managers and Product Teams

 External Key Stakeholders – Clients, Investment Managers, Regulators including CBoI

 
 Skills/Experience 
 The successful candidate will benefit from having: 
 Experience within Financial Services/Asset Servicing/Fund Administration is desirable but not essential.

 Experience of working with teams in multiple locations as part of an outsourced arrangement is desirable but not essential.

 Ability to build strong relationships with external clients.

 Self-motivated, innovative and analytical.

 Strong time management and organisational skills.

 Excellent communication and interpersonal skills are essential.

 Strong ability to analyse data and identify errors.

 Demonstrates commitment to producing professional and very high-quality work in tight timelines.

 
 Work Authorization 

 Applicants must have the right to work in Ireland at the time of application and for the duration of employment.

 Please note that Northern Trust is unable to provide employment permit sponsorship for this role. This includes Critical Skills Employment Permits, General Employment Permits, Intra-Company Transfer Employment Permits, Stamp 1G permissions, and other employment permits under Irish immigration frameworks.

 Working with Us

Movement within the organization is encouraged, senior leaders are accessible, and you can take pride in working for a company committed to an inclusive workplace and assisting the communities we serve. 

 Philanthropy is deeply rooted in Northern Trust’s history and is an essential element of our culture. Employees around the world give their time and talent to work for the greater good of their communities. 

 Reasonable Accommodation 

 Northern Trust is committed to working with and providing adjustments to individuals with health conditions and disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please email our HR Service Center at MyHRHelp@ntrs.com , or alternatively you can discuss your individual requirements with the recruiter you are working with.

title: Supply Planner
description:
Work Flexibility: Hybrid 
 
 Initial 12 Month FTC 
 
 Supply Planner - Limerick 
 Hybrid or Onsite (3 day onsite requirement)
 
 Who we want 
 • Detail-oriented process improvers . Critical thinkers who naturally see opportunities to develop and optimize work processes – finding ways to simplify, standardize and automate.
 • Collaborative partners. People who build and leverage cross-functional relationships to bring together ideas, data and insights to drive continuous improvement in functions.
 • Strategic thinkers . People who enjoy analyzing data or trends for the purposes of planning, forecasting, advising, budgeting, reporting, or sales opportunities.
 
 Role Summary 
 The role will interface with production scheduling, procurement, and customer service to ensure an integrated approach to supply planning within the franchise and take the lead in responding to the demand requirements from the business and ensuring that there is supply plan in place to communicate what needs to be produced and purchased to the manufacturing and supply base within the franchise.
 
 Main Duties & Responsibilities 
 Support the creation of a Master Resource Plan based on the latest demand signal to cover what needs to be produced or purchased as a finished product and to ensure that within the process there is sufficient raw materials and components to support the required supply plan up to a 24-month time horizon

 Support the creation of capacity plans based on the latest demand signal to identify where there are potential bottlenecks or risks to supply and to develop and recommend appropriate proposals to mitigate and to ensure that the plant or 3rd party can meet the future demand. Also identify where there is significant underutilization which could impact the costs of supply.

 Responsibility will be initially scoped to limited number of products /segments of the portfolio and during development phase the individual would be closely monitored and coached into supply planning

 Work under the supervision of the Supply Planning manager in Setting of the correct levels of inventory (safety stocks) within the supply plan by understanding the demand volatility and supply chain lead times

 Tracking of the execution of the supply plan with production scheduling and buying ensuring that the plan is fully operationalized and tracked for performance deviation including mitigation on back orders and pro-active communication of future supply risks.

 Ensuring within the supply plan that products are being phased in and planned correctly as well as ensuring communication and timing of exiting products within the plant or 3rd party. Communicating with the business in regard to the status of the product portfolio from a supply planning perspective.

 Support the Supply Planning Manager in providing effective communication and confirmation back from supply planning to the demand plan in confirming capability to meet the requirements via the daily and weekly execution process but also via a robust monthly executive supply process.

 All Supply Planning system core master-data is maintained to enable focus on real supply issues

 KPIs for the role will be Supply Plan Attainment, Safety Stock Health, Capacity Utilization, Back order and Lead time

 Responsible for root causing performance issues and providing recommendation to Supply Planning Manager /leader on how to mitigate and sustain.

 
 Education & Skills Required 
 Level 8 Degree in Business/Engineering/Supply Chain management

 Minimum of 2 years in either a production, supply or demand planning role where knowledge is demonstrated and experience gained in planning 

 Excellent knowledge of MS Excel

 Strong attention to detail, able to analyze and make sense of large amounts of data that can be presented back to operations.

 Experience in a manufacturing environment would be beneficial

 
   
  
 Ireland Pay Ranges: Ireland : €47,000 - €77,000 EUR Annual
 
   
  
 At Stryker, we believe transparency helps candidates make confident decisions about their next career step. Compensation is an important part of that process and we want to be clear about how pay is determined. The compensation information posted for this role may be presented as a salary range or a fixed amount depending on the role.  In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for incentive compensation (such as bonus and/or commissions where applicable), along with Stryker’s comprehensive benefits package.
  
 If you’d like to learn more about the salary or the benefits associated with this role, your recruiter will be happy to walk you through the details as you progress through the hiring process.
   
  
Travel Percentage: 10%

Transaction Analyst 
 Full-time, Permanent 
 Hybrid - 3 Days Onsite 
 Dublin, Ireland 
  
 
 The Position 
   
 A Transaction Analyst (TA) reports to a Manager of the Governance & Transaction Services team and will have responsibility for the legal, corporate and administrative affairs relating to a portfolio of clients within the Capital Markets team. The proposed salary range for this position is €30,000 to €35,000 gross per annum. The final salary will be determined based on the successful candidate's skills, qualifications and experience, while also taking into account internal equity and our commitment to a fair, consistent and gender-neutral compensation framework.
 
 
 Key Responsibilities 

   
 Assisting in ensuring all on-going statutory, legal and transactional obligations of the SPVs we manage, in structured finance and securitisation deals, are met and ensuring good corporate governance throughout.
 Assisting with the coordination and oversight of pan-European securitisation transactions from a governance, compliance and administrative perspective.
 Assisting with organising, convening (including the preparation of board packs) and attending client board and committee meetings. Drafting minutes and action item lists from board and committee meetings and circulating to clients and boards of directors in a timely manner.
 Assisting with monitoring the obligations and client deadlines of the team.
 Maintaining statutory registers, filing forms with the CRO, incorporating new companies, and processing dissolutions.
 Complete the take-on of new clients, including ensuring AML is completed in accordance with CSC’s internal policies
 Arranging for document execution and liaising with intermediaries for the safe delivery of such documents within a quick turnaround.
 Completing KYC processes and preparing documents.

 Key Competencies 
  
 Bachelor’s degree with a minimum 2:1 grade in a Legal, Finance or Business degree or similar

 Excellent attention to detail is essential.

Role Review: Financial Accountant
Mason Alexander • July 19, 2019
​What is a Financial Accountant?
The traditional role of a Financial Accountant is to record, summarise and report on the myriad of transactions resulting from business operations over a period of time. Ultimately, these transactions are summarised in the preparation of financial statements, including the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement, the records of the company’s financial performance over a specified period. But in reality, the role of a Financial Accountant can be broad and varied depending on the industry in which you work in. A Financial Accountant in an SME can have many different responsibilities to that of a peer in a large company or PLC.
How to secure a Financial Accountant role:
Practice Route
In order to become a Financial Accountant, you can complete a training contract with a recognised training accounting firm. These range from the “Big 4” firms to mid-tier and right down to small, local firms. In Ireland, this typically results in a training contract to complete the exams of Chartered Accountants Ireland and to become an ACA. Training in practice as an ACCA is also widely available though the firms that offer this tend to be smaller in size.
Industry
An alternative option to the practice route is training in Industry. ACCA are the market leaders when it comes to training in industry but Chartered Accountants offer their Flexible Route option which get you the same qualification as going the practice route and there is also CPA. Traditionally you will start as an accounts assistant while studying towards your qualification. You will then graduate to a financial accountant role once your qualifications have been gained. It can sometimes take a little longer to qualified within industry as the opportunity for study leave is limited as you balance fulltime work and study but the opportunity to break down the exams into smaller, more manageable segments is a key benefit of this route.
The experience gained from training in industry will equip you with the hands on skills to confidently transition into a financial accountant role and the steep learning curve of those transitioning from practice to industry is not experienced.
Future career prospects with this experience:
There a few professions that are as global and universally recognised as accountancy, the world is your oyster! Upon gaining experience as a financial accountant there are many opportunities to progress your career. If the finance side is where you see your strengths and attributes flourishing, you can progress to Senior Accountant, Finance Business Partner, Finance Manager, Financial Controller, Director right through to C-Suite (CFO/CEO).
This experience can also allow you to move internally to the commercial side of the business such as business partnering, financial planning and analysis and commercial analyst roles. With this, you will be responsible for providing senior management and executives with analysis and information to make key operational, financial and strategic decisions. These moves allow for more commercial exposure and open up a wider range of potential future roles.
Salary Range
﻿ €45,000 – €60,000 DOE

Job Description:
Dołączenie do firmy Vistra jeszcze nigdy nie było tak ekscytujące!
W Vistra naszym celem jest postęp. Wierzymy, że nasi klienci mają moc zmieniania świata i robienia wielkich rzeczy dla globalnego postępu. Istniejemy po to, aby usuwać przeszkody wynikające z zawiłości globalnego biznesu, a także, by pomagać naszym klientom osiągać postęp.
Postęp może wydarzyć się tylko wtedy, gdy ludzie zjednoczą się i podejmą działania. Jesteśmy absolutnie zaangażowani w budowanie kultury, w której nasi pracownicy mogą to robić.
Mamy dla Ciebie świetną propozycję, aby dołączyć do naszego zespołu jako  Tax Assistant,  na stałe, w wymiarze pełnego etatu. Praca zlokalizowana jest w Polsce (Warszawa) i daje możliwość przyczynienia się do rozwoju naszego działu  Tax .
Zakres obowiązków:
Wspieranie specjalistów podatkowych Vistra w wykonywanych przez nich zadaniach
Udział w przygotowywaniu opinii podatkowych
Pomoc przy przygotowywaniu dokumentacji cen transferowych
Wyszukiwanie i analiza informacji (przepisy podatkowe, prasa i literatura fachowa)
Dokonywanie przeglądu orzecznictwa i interpretacji z zakresu prawa podatkowego oraz monitorowanie zmian w przepisach podatkowych
Przygotowywanie nieskomplikowanych tłumaczeń
Wsparcie administracyjne
Wymagania:
Zainteresowanie prawem podatkowym i co najmniej teoretyczna wiedza w tym zakresie
Wykształcenie wyższe prawnicze lub ekonomiczne, ewentualnie ostatni rok studiów
Bardzo dobra znajomość języka angielskiego
Umiejętność analizy i interpretacji przepisów prawa
Dobra znajomość pakietu MS Office, w szczególności Word i Excel
Umiejętność analitycznego myślenia, samodzielność i bardzo dobra organizacja pracy
Co oferujemy:
Zdrowie pracowników jest dla nas ważne – otrzymasz możliwość dofinansowania do prywatnej opieki medycznej dla Ciebie i Twoich bliskich.
Dbamy o zdrowy tryb życia i aktywność sportową – otrzymasz możliwość dofinansowania do karty Multisport.
Jeżeli tak jak my cenisz sobie work-life balance, to zapewne ucieszy Cię, że umożliwiamy elastyczne godziny pracy.
Ważne jest dla Ciebie bezpieczeństwo? Otrzymasz możliwość wykupienia dodatkowego ubezpieczenia na życie.
Ponieważ chcemy wspierać Twój rozwój, umożliwimy Ci dołączenie na bezpłatne lekcje z języka angielskiego lub niemieckiego.
Gwarantujemy stabilność zatrudnienia: umowa o pracę z firmą działającą globalnie, o ugruntowanej pozycji na rynku.
Ponieważ najważniejszy jest dla nas Twój rozwój zawodowy, zapewnimy szkolenia wewnętrzne, a także dofinansowanie do szkoleń zewnętrznych lub studiów podyplomowych, a także jasną ścieżka kariery Vistra.
Mając na uwadze Twoją wygodę oraz oszczędność czasu, nasze nowoczesne biuro jest zlokalizowane w centrum miasta.
Jesteśmy świadomi ekologicznie: adoptujemy pszczoły, zachęcamy pracowników do przyjeżdżania rowerem (mamy rowerowy parking!), a nasz budynek jest eco-friendly.

Skip to main content Kickstart Your Career Journey with Azets
At Azets, we celebrate everyone’s individual story, home lives, hobbies and ambitions and we have a place for them all. We believe that diversity and flexibility is essential to creating a modern, vibrant and successful culture – one where being yourself and doing the best work of your life goes hand in hand.
Kickstart your career journey with Azets
If you're a graduate just starting out, eager to learn, grow, and make an impact, this is the perfect place to begin your journey. We know that launching your career can be both exciting and challenging, but here, you'll be supported every step of the way. You'll gain hands-on experience, develop valuable skills, and be part of a team that values your contributions. You might love numbers, but you will never be just a number.
Hear what our Associates have to say
The Azets Academy
Azets Ireland are excited to announce the launch of our new Azets Academy. As a graduate, the Academy will offer you a state of the art, 3 ½ year training programme to learn, grow and develop. Our graduates have first-hand access to our partners and senior management, backing your ambition on your journey to becoming a fully qualified accountant. The Academy will also offer  international travel , granting you access to develop and network around our different offices across Europe.
Incoming graduates in Azets Ireland work collaboratively in a three and half year programme in our business. Backed by supportive and experienced colleagues, graduates work with our clients from the very beginning, giving them the opportunity to build strong relationships.
For the new graduate, our culture and values permeate through everything we do, ensuring a supportive learning environment as you progress. Our people are key to the firm’s success. We put people first, resulting in a workforce that prides itself on going the extra mile for our clients.
Azets
At Azets people are at the core of what we do, with trainees being the first important building block in our success. We are extremely proud of and value the expertise and technical know-how within our business, but we equally understand the importance of enhancing and sharing this knowledge to continuously develop our future workforce.
With the everchanging economic landscape and advances in technology, there has never been a more exciting time to start a career in accountancy. Whether a school/college leaver, a graduate or simply looking for a career change, why not start your journey here at Azets?
We are committed to offering development opportunities to all of our staff, from Entry Level Trainee through to Senior Partner. As a trainee, all of our roles will provide a professional qualification specific to the business area you will be working in.
The role
As part of your role as an Associate Graduate Trainee, you will be working with as part of a knowledgeable and experienced team to learn everything possible in the world of accounting. You will be supported in your development and will be encouraged to expand your experience as much as possible.
Key Requirements
To get the job that you’ll love you will:
Have the right to work in Ireland from your start date
Undergraduate degree in finance, accounting or related discipline
Be on track to achieve or have already achieved a minimum 2:1 in your undergraduate degree
Azets - Our Development Programme
We have created a first-class training and development programme and, by starting your career at Azets, in addition to the comprehensive on the job training, you will also be given all the support you need to complete a professional qualification, including college and/or study days, mentoring and a designated buddy.
We offer a range of different qualification pathways at Azets which are determined by the role you are applying for.
For us, the personal attributes of each of our employees are what makes us authentic in the marketplace. We look for people who can collaborate with peers and can also bring their own voice to the table. We want people who are dynamic in their approach and respectful of other people’s opinions. We are looking for someone who wants to be more than just a team member, rather someone who wants to join a family of like minded individuals.
Compliance assurance
Reduce risk of errors and penalties with accurate, timely submissions.
Flexible solutions
Whether you are an SME or a large employer, we tailor our services to your workforce and payroll complexity.
We are ready to help
With over 300 colleagues and 4 offices in Dublin, Sandyford, Enniscorthy and Belfast, Azets is part of a team of 9,000 talented, smart people across our international office network. Offering a personal, local approach to supporting Irish businesses, if you’re looking for peace of mind, expert advice and more time, we’re ready to help.

title: 2027 Graduate Instrument Planner - Orthopedics
description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com .
 
 As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.
 
 
 Job Function: 
Supply Chain Planning 
 
 Job Sub Function: 
Supply Network Planning 
 
 Job Category: 
Professional 
 
 All Job Posting Locations: 
Cork, Cork, Ireland, Ringaskiddy, Cork, Ireland 
 
 Job Description: 
 
 
 ROLE TITLE: Graduate Instrument Planner
 START DATE: September 2027
 LOCATION: Cork, Ireland
 
 Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopaedics business to establish a standalone orthopaedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes 
 
 DePuy Synthes, Companies of Johnson & Johnson , is the largest, most comprehensive orthopedic and neurological business in the world, built upon the strong legacies of two great companies. 
 
 DePuy Synthes offer an unparalleled breadth and depth of technology, devices, services and programs in the areas of joint reconstruction, trauma, spine, sports medicine, neurological, cranio-maxillofacial, power tools and biomaterials. 
 
 Our broad array of inspired, innovative and high-quality offerings helps advance the health and well-being of people around the world. 
 DePuy Synthes, who employ over 1000 people in Cork established its manufacturing facility in Cork in 1997 where it manufactures orthopedic knees and hips. In 2014, DePuy Synthes in Cork won the Shingo Prize for Operational Excellence.
 
 
 POSITION SUMMARY: 
 The Graduate Planner within the Instruments Deployment Group is a key supply chain role, we provide a world class service to our Direct and Affiliate Global markets for the Joints Business Group. The team is also responsible for instrument set planning and governance for OUS markets.
 
 
 ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 
 Customer Orders/Requests: 
 Receive and respond to customer orders/requests.

 Will enter orders into the relevant ERP system.

 Research, resolve, and follow through with customer issues/complaints, deal with adverse situations, make effective decisions promptly and inform key partners appropriately.

 Will respond to questions relating to delivery information, credit authorization, pricing, and product specific service-related questions.

 Will liaise with supply partners to obtain and communicate delivery information, sharing information on priorities.

 
 Deliver Effective and Efficient Planning: 
 Ensure planned kit requirements and supplemental order processes are completed accurately and in line with global planning 

 Work with warehouse to manage stock queries, expedite outbound/inbound deliveries and coordinate activity between markets 

 Investigate and root-cause critical supply issues and communicate updates on resolution dates 

 Inventory management in line with agreed GSC targets and processes – taking actions to minimize excess inventory, including managing inventory repatriation, and approving in market returns 

 Drive for continuous improvement to enhance service and implement lean process improvements.

 Coordinate the implementation of New Product Introductions/ Rationalization plans with OUS Markets in line with commercial and project teams.

 
 Market Service Review & Performance Analysis: 
 Represent market supply needs and challenges within the Sales & Operations Planning process.

 Will support ongoing improvements to supply chain efficiency by working closely with markets and monitoring market behaviour with a focus to enhance overall “end customer” service. 

 Proactively manage KPI’s, including OTIF, back-order metrics and ad-hoc process improvement metrics.

 Develop and strengthen team relationships with external and internal customers in accordance with our Instrument Deployment Group, GSC, and Depuy goals and objectives. 

 Initiate & maintain reports and support projects as required.

 Will support the development of Team members through training & coaching

 
 
 EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE: 
 Essential: 
 Minimum Bachelors degree in   Business, Supply Chain, Logistics  or similar   degree

 Recent Graduate ( 2026  or due to graduate in  2027 )

 Continuous Improvement / Lean Manufacturing systems concept knowledge

 The ability to work well individually and remotely.

 The ability to adapt to change and develop skills to meet these changes.

 High capability with Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc.)

 Interest in developing skills, abilities, and career.

 Pro-active, can-do attitude. High level of personal initiative, ability to function autonomously and self-confidence.

 Self-starter with ability to create and develop new relationships quickly, and   influence/collaborate   to get to desired results.

 Results Orientation/Sense of Urgency – ability to drive to tight timelines.

 Data mining / reporting skills.

 Exposure to Project Management Methodology would be an advantage

 Interested in Manufacturing processes.

 
 
 
 
 
  
  
 Required Skills: 
  
  
 Preferred Skills: 
   
  
 The anticipated base pay range for this position is: 
€34,800.00 - €55,775.00  
  
 Benefits: 
 In addition to base pay, we offer the following benefits*: an annual bonus with set target (% of pay) depending on pay grade / location, where the actual amount is based on the employees’ and companies’ performance of the previous calendar year, or sales commissions. Moreover, we offer vacation days, parental leave for a minimum of 12 weeks, bereavement leave, caregiver leave, volunteer leave, well-being reimbursement, programs for financial, physical and mental health. We also offer service anniversary and recognition awards, and subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees - and in some location’s eligible dependents - can participate in several insurance plans. For more information, visit Employee benefits | Supporting well-being & career growth | Johnson & Johnson Careers. 
  
 *This is for informative purposes only. Amounts and actual benefits may vary by location and are subject to change.

_____________________________________________________________________
COMPANY AND ROLE BACKGROUND
Ornua is a leading dairy co-operative which sells premium dairy products globally on behalf of its Member Co-operatives, Ireland’s dairy processors and, in turn, Irish dairy farmers.
Ornua has revenues of €3.4 billion and is supported by a global team of approximately 2,800 employees. The Group operates as a commercial organisation across 10 business units, including 12 production facilities located in Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa.
The commercial organisation is responsible for the marketing and sales of Ornua’s consumer brands including Ireland’s most successful food export: Kerrygold. Consumer markets are served by production facilities in Ireland, Germany and the UK and by in-market Sales & Marketing Teams in Asia, Germany, Ireland, MEA, Poland, Spain, rest of Europe and North and Latin America.
It also manages the procurement of Irish and non-Irish dairy products, the sale of dairy ingredients to food manufacturing and foodservice customers globally, and the implementation of de-risking and trading strategies to manage market volatility. These activities are supported by production facilities and in-market teams in Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa.
The Role:
An opportunity has now arisen for a Financial Accountant to join the Dublin Co-Op team.   The successful candidate will have responsibility and accountability for the following areas:
Key Areas of Responsibility:
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements
Perform balance sheet reconciliations and investigate variances
Support month-end and year-end close processes
Ensure compliance with accounting standards
Inventory Valuation analysis
Assist in audits and liaise with external auditors
Manage general ledger and journal entries
Support budgeting and forecasting processes
Improve financial controls and processes
Ad Hoc reporting
Key Requirements/Attributes:
Recently qualified Chartered Accountant (ACA) with Big 4 experience
Good team player with strong communication and interpersonal skills
Commercially astute with strong analytical skills
Strong attention to detail
Highly motivated and dynamic – ability to work to deadlines and achieve targets in a time-conscious manner
Good IT skills, particularly Excel and AI
Practical and common-sense approach to problem solving, and the ability to demonstrate creative solutions
Experience with cost accounting, or monitoring and measuring sales performance is an advantage
Additional Benefits
Leave 25 days pro rata  plus 2.5 company days (half day Xmas eve, 29 December, Good Friday)
Pension
Two weeks work from anywhere
Hybrid working (3 days in office)
Summer hours
Subsidised canteen
Free breakfast dinner on Friday
Free parking onsite (booking system)
EAP Scheme for employee and immediate family
Life Assurance salary
Long term illness benefit
Paternity benefit/Maternity benefit
Phased return from Maternity leave
Closing date: Friday 4th September

title: Learning & Development Specialist (12 month contract)
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Abbott in Ireland 
 Operating since 1946, Abbott serves the Irish market with a diverse range of healthcare products. We employ around 6,000 people across ten sites in Dublin, Donegal, Clonmel, Cootehill, Galway, Kilkenny, Longford, and Sligo.
 
 Abbott Diabetes Care Division Donegal 
 The Abbott Diabetes Care division based in Donegal Town manufactures FreeStyle blood glucose test strips and FreeStyle Sensors for use in diabetes management. Among Abbott Diabetes Care leading brands are the FreeStyle Precision, FreeStyle Lite and FreeStyle Libre system.
 
 Please note any offer of employment for this position is conditional upon the successful completion of a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening, conducted by a medical practitioner designated by the Company
 
 Overview 
 Reporting to the Operational Excellence Manager, the Learning & Development Specialist will lead and coordinate the site's Learning & Development agenda, supporting the delivery of ADC Donegal's Learning & Development Strategy, workforce capability initiatives, talent development programmes, and Operational Excellence learning activities.
 
 The successful candidate will work closely with Site Leadership, HR, managers and employees across all functions to build a future-ready workforce through structured learning, leadership development, continuous improvement and career development initiatives.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Support the execution of the ADC Donegal Learning & Development Strategy, aligning capability-building initiatives with workforce planning, business priorities and the site's 2028 vision.

 Promote a culture of continuous learning through engaging communications, site-wide development initiatives and effective use of AD Connect and other communication channels.

 Manage the end-to-end delivery of learning and development programmes, including planning, stakeholder engagement, communications, certification, reporting and continuous improvement.

 Coordinate and support talent, leadership and early career development programmes to strengthen organisational capability and succession pipelines.

 Lead the coordination and continuous improvement of the Lean Six Sigma Academy, including Yellow Belt, Green Belt and Operational Excellence development programmes.

 Conduct capability assessments and learning needs analyses, partnering with stakeholders to identify development priorities, performance gaps and targeted learning solutions.

 Support the development of capability frameworks, learning pathways and future skills strategies that enable employee growth and organisational effectiveness.

 Build and maintain relationships with training providers, educational institutions and industry partners to enhance workforce development opportunities.

 Coordinate external funding initiatives, including IDA-funded training programmes, ensuring effective administration, compliance, reporting and audit readiness.

 Manage learning systems, programme metrics and evaluation processes, using data and learner feedback to measure effectiveness, demonstrate value and drive continuous improvement.

 
 Education & Experience 
 Third-level qualification in Learning & Development, Human Resources, Business, Organisational Development or a related discipline is desirable.

 Minimum of 6 years' experience working within a Learning & Development, Human Resources, Organisational Development or business environment with a strong Learning & Development focus.

 Experience facilitating workshops, development programmes or training interventions.

 Excellent communication, facilitation and stakeholder management abilities, Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills.

 Ability to manage multiple priorities and programmes simultaneously.

 Experience with Microsoft Forms, SharePoint, Power BI and learning technologies.

About Servaada, a Wipro company:
Servaada is Wipro UK entity, authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), the UK financial services regulator,  to undertake regulated activities on behalf of its clients, as an outsourced service provider.
Job Description:
Role Purpose
This new role establishes the Line 1.5 Investment Administration Risk & Controls function, acting as the operational and analytical bridge between Investment Administration (1LOD) and Compliance (2LOD). The role manages market surveillance, daily controls, reconciliations oversight, reporting, and analytics to ensure all relevant controls are executed before escalation.
Line 1, Line 1.5, and 2LOD Responsibilities
Line 1.5 owns the execution, first‑level review, and documentation of IA and surveillance controls; Line 1 owns operational processing; and 2LOD provides independent oversight and challenge.
This role ensures timely analysis, triage, and escalation, providing structured challenge and insight across IA, Trading Support, Technology, Clients, and Risk functions.
Key Responsibilities
1. Market Surveillance, Controls Operation & Daily Oversight
Execute and document the daily market‑surveillance control suite (price moves, DTV anomalies, news adjacency, peer alignment, liquidity shifts).
Perform first‑level analysis of surveillance alerts, investigate exceptions, and escalate issues promptly where thresholds or patterns indicate concern.
Identify behaviours, anomalies, or themes requiring 2LOD or senior‑management escalation.
2. Reconciliation Oversight
• Oversee all 2‑way and 3‑way reconciliations across positions, pricing, market data, and broker/internal feeds, consolidating break analysis into a single oversight process.
Conduct root‑cause analysis for breaks, provide challenge to IA teams, and ensure appropriate escalation and closure.
3. Reporting, Analytics & Monthly Look‑Back Reviews
Produce daily IA control MI, reconciliation oversight MI, and market‑surveillance analytics.
Lead monthly thematic look‑backs across price behaviours, reconciliation trends, liquidity events, or news‑driven patterns.
Maintain dashboards for IA governance, 2LOD reporting, JRCC, COWG, Board Packs, and Quarterly Compliance MI
4. Investment Administration & Market Operations Expertise
Interpret market events affecting IA (corporate actions, liquidity events, price volatility) and support decision‑making with data‑based insights.
Provide analytical challenge to IA and Trading Support to strengthen operational execution and reduce control failures.
5. Risk Management & Governance
Maintain the IA risk register and control inventory, ensuring clarity of ownership and control frequency.
Identify gaps and drive automation or enhancement of IA controls and data quality.
Ensure clear, timely MI and commentary for 2LOD oversight, senior governance, and client reporting.
6. Stakeholder Engagement
Act as the central coordinating point between IA, Compliance, Technology, Clients, Vendors, and Risk.
Communicate issues, insights, and trends clearly and constructively to stakeholders.
Required Skills & Experience
Strong knowledge of IA, market operations, and UK MAR surveillance indicators.
Experience with control operation, reconciliations, and market‑data analysis.
Strong analytical skills (Excel, modelling, market data) and ability to produce clear MI and challenge.
Excellent communication and the ability to constructively challenge internal and external stakeholders.
Qualifications
Degree in Finance, Economics, Risk, or related discipline (preferred).
Professional certifications desirable (CISI IOC, IMC, surveillance/compliance modules).
3–5+ years in IA, surveillance, risk, trading support, or middle office.
Success Measures (First 6–12 Months)
Effective, timely execution and documentation of daily market surveillance controls.
Strong oversight of reconciliations, with improved turnaround and reduced breaks.
Embedded monthly look‑back reporting with actionable insights.
Clear definition of Line 1 vs 1.5 vs 2LOD responsibilities.
Improved control environment, reduced breaches, and strong audit outcomes.
Equal Opportunities:
Servaada is committed to diversity, equality, and inclusion in the workplace. All applicants welcome.
