title: Graduate Software Engineer
description:
About Wayflyer 
 Today's small businesses need a capital provider that keeps pace with their growth ambitions. Traditional financing options are slow, cumbersome and often out of reach. That's why we built Wayflyer.
 Our technology allows us to assess businesses in minutes, generate financing offers that reflect their growth potential, and send funds in as little as 24 hours. To date, we've deployed over $6bn to thousands of businesses worldwide, backed by Tier 1 banks like J.P. Morgan.
 You'll be collaborating with ambitious colleagues from around the world. We have offices in Dublin, London, New York, Charlotte, Berlin and Sydney.
 The challenge 
 Every founder who applies for funding moves through one connected system, from the data that assesses their business in minutes, to the product experience that makes getting funded feel effortless. As a graduate engineer, you won't just be handed a slice of that system to maintain. You'll get exposure to the whole thing: the data model, the API, the screen a founder trusts with their business, and the room to figure out where you want to go deep.
 What you'll actually do 
 Own features end-to-end: work with product and design to shape solutions, build them, and ship to production, creating outcomes, not just closing tickets

 Write clean, testable code with comprehensive unit and integration tests

 Build new features that drive revenue and engagement, while keeping the lights on for what's already live

 Participate in code reviews and contribute to technical documentation

 Push technical discussions forward and raise the bar on quality, rather than waiting to be told what "good" looks like

 Every feature you ship has a real person behind it, a founder waiting on funding, a brand trying to grow, so the way you build matters as much as what you build.
 What this role could turn into 
 Engineers who bring this kind of ownership tend not to stay in one lane for long. Some grow into technical leads shaping how we build across teams. Others move into product-adjacent roles, working even closer with the businesses we serve. And some end up specialising deep into the systems and infrastructure that let us scale globally. Where you go depends on what you're curious about.

 You're a curious builder who gets genuine satisfaction from turning a messy idea into something people actually use. You ask questions before you assume, communicate clearly when something's not working, and take ownership without needing permission for every step. You're comfortable in ambiguity, you'd rather experiment and learn than wait for the perfect brief, and how you treat people matters to you as much as the code you ship.

 Hands-on experience with Python, React (or similar), and SQL/relational databases

 Bonus, not required: exposure to REST APIs, testing frameworks, CI/CD, cloud, or containerisation

 Location and working policy 
 Based in our Dublin HQ. Hybrid, 3-4 days onsite to start, transitioning to a more flexible remote role over time.
Please note we are hiring for a start date in June 2027.
 The good stuff 
 25 days annual leave plus public holidays, private healthcare, life insurance and critical illness cover, a pension plan, generous parental leave, equity, and the option to work from abroad for up to 60 days a year.

title: Core Operations - Officer
description:
Who we are looking for 
 
 We are looking for an individual with good Custody knowledge and a proven track record of dealing with and managing large client relationships in the Custody Department. . Knowledge of financial products, Financial markets, Custody Operations (including market settlements, Global payments, Corporate events, Global sub custody networks) is required. The candidate should be client focused, organised, possess a strong work ethic. Working as part of a dedicated client Custody Management team the candidate should be experienced in all aspects of Client management while ensuring that State Streets Ethical, Compliance and Risk Mangement principals are at all times adhered to 
 The role requires experience working in a highly matrixed environment and a good understanding of all aspects of operational perspectives.
 
 
 Why this role is important to us 
 
 The team you will be joining is a key part of State Street Global Delivery (SSGD) organisation 
 SSGD gives Global asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping, to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGD’ tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities. 
 Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for. 
 
 What you will be responsible for 
 The CMS Officer is responsible for supporting the delivery of high-quality custody services to assigned institutional clients, acting as a key coordination point between clients, investment managers, operations, and internal and external support functions. The role combines client service, operational oversight, issue resolution, risk management, and service governance responsibilities to ensure the consistent delivery of custody services in accordance with State Street's control framework and client service standards.
 The successful candidate will develop strong client relationships, monitor operational performance, identify and escalate risks, and drive timely resolution of service issues while contributing to a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence.
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Client Service and Relationship Management 
 
 Strong team player who can work on own initiative with minimum supervision
 Act as a primary contact for designated Global custody clients and investment managers.
 Manage day-to-day client service inquiries and operational escalations.
 Coordinate responses in a timely manner across operations, asset servicing, settlements, cash processing, onboarding, fund accounting, and other support teams.
 Build and maintain effective relationships with clients, internal stakeholders, and service delivery teams.
 Support the preparation and delivery of client service reviews and governance meetings.
 Governance and Reporting 
 Prepare management information, service dashboards, and client reporting packs.
 Support internal governance forums and client service governance meetings.
 Maintain accurate records of service issues, action items, and client commitments.
 Contribute to KPI, KRI, and service performance reporting.
 Assist with regulatory, audit, and compliance activities relating to custody servicing.
 New Business and Change Management 
 Support onboarding of new funds, clients, and investment managers.
 Participate in operational readiness activities for new products, markets, and regulatory initiatives.
 Assist with testing, implementation, and communication activities associated with system and process enhancements.
 Continuous Improvement 
 Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, client experience, and risk management.
 Participate in process reviews and improvement initiatives.
 Support automation and simplification of manual processes where appropriate.
 Contribute to the enhancement of CMS procedures, controls, and best practices.
 Education & Preferred Qualifications 
 University Degree or equivalent experience,
  5- 7 years of experience in the Banking and Financial Services  business
 Strong understanding of operational processes across all aspects of Global Custody
 
 About State Street 
 What we do. State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation, we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.
 Work, Live and Grow. We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary by location, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans, among other perks. You’ll have access to flexible Work Programs to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.
 Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility. We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. We warmly welcome candidates of diverse origin, background, ability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and personality. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. You will have tools to help balance your professional and personal life, paid volunteer days, matching gift programs and access to employee networks that help you stay connected to what matters to you.
 State Street is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer.
 Discover more at StateStreet.com/careers
 
 
 
 About State Street 
 Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
 
 We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.
 
 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

 We believe it’s urgent to deliver medical solutions right now – even as we develop innovations for the future. We are passionate about transforming patients’ lives. We are courageous in both decision and action. We believe that good business means a better world. That is why we come to work each day. We commit ourselves to scientific rigour, unassailable ethics, and access to medical innovations for all. We do this today to build a better tomorrow. 
 We are proud of who we are, what we do, and how we do it. We are many, working as one across functions, across companies, and across the world. 
 We are Roche. 
 
 About the Role: 
 
 Roche Products (Ireland) Limited is the sales & marketing arm in Ireland 
 of the pharmaceutical division of Roche. We market and sell prescription medicines across a range of therapeutic areas including oncology, neurology, ophthalmology, rheumatology and spinal muscular atrophy. We are an agile organisation that brings together great people who are passionate about innovation, and who thrive in dynamic, cross-functional, and purposeful teams. These teams work together to deliver outstanding value to our business, patients, and customers. 
 
 This role is working within the Finance & Business Operations team which includes Finance, Supply Chain, Quality, Procurement, Business Support and Administration. The team provides support across the business and you will be working with multiple stakeholders. 
 
 
 In this role you require a broad set of skills in communication, interpersonal relationships, managing a diverse workload and an ability to manage your time effectively. Comfortable working both as a part of a team as well as on your own initiative, you will have proven organisational capability & high levels of personal effectiveness. You will be a self starte, have a flexible and adaptable approach to work and will be experienced working across the MS Windows and Google platforms.  
 
 The role will be based in our office in Citywest in Dublin . 
 Salary:   36605.00 - 57150.00 Euro Annually 
 Hours per week:   35 
 
 What you could be working on: 
 
 You will ensure operational excellence by delivering seamless front-of-house management, comprehensive executive support, and efficient facility and procurement services. This central liaison role maintains rigorous compliance and process consistency, empowering leadership and cross-functional teams to achieve their business objectives. You work will include the following: 
 Validating employee expenses via Concur, both credit card and cash expenses – checking coding, mileage claims, etc. 
 Managing and optimising the General Manager’s complex calendar, prioritising sensitive and time-critical meetings 
 Coordinating logistics for senior-level meetings, board meetings and Town Halls 
 Managing front-of-house office operations, acting as the primary point of contact for all site visitors to ensure a professional workplace experience and executive-level standards 
 Acting as the first point of contact for incoming inquiries, directing calls and correspondence to appropriate teams to maintain efficient cross-functional workflows 
 Liaising with RDT (Roche Digital Technologies), P&C (People & Culture), Finance and other teams to coordinate and support day-to-day business operations 
 Maintain the Finance & Business Operations intranet page and update information in consultation with relevant stakeholders 
 Supporting the Procurement Manager with supplier selection, including Requests for PO, tender processes and the subsequent management of appointed suppliers 
 Maintaining procurement contracts, raising purchase orders as required and managing preferred-supplier lists 
 Supporting the Procurement Manager in sourcing Company cars and maintain comprehensive documentation for the Company car fleet 
 Supporting the day-to-day operation of facilities and coordinating related vendor and contractor activities 
 Providing support to the Disease Area Squads to include; Organising events ranging from conferences to product launches, including vendor coordination 
 Supporting stakeholder and customer engagement activities as directed by the Squad Lead 
 Tracking and reporting on work-package progress 
 Creating templates and processes to support standardisation across squads 
 Supporting the consistent use of mandatory tools, including Techsuite 
 Arranging meetings and planning sessions, including Reviews, Retrospectives, Planning and Connect sessions 
 Sharing best practices with colleagues supporting other squads 
 
 
 
 Essential Qualifications: 
 
 The ideal candidate will ideally be educated to diploma or degree level and have 3-5 years experience in a similar role. 
 
   
   
 
 Who we are A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
 
Let’s build a healthier future, together.
 
 Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Customer Care Specialist
About Kerry
Kerry is the world's leading taste and nutrition company for the food, beverage and pharmaceutical industries. Every day we partner with customers to create healthier, tastier and more sustainable products that are consumed by billions of people across the world. Our vision is to be our customers' most valued partner, creating a world of sustainable nutrition. A career with Kerry offers you an opportunity to shape the future of food while providing you opportunities to explore and grow in a truly global environment.
About the role
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced, passionate and professional individual, with the ability to operate in a dynamic environment to join our Customer Care team as a French or Polish speaking Customer Care Specialist.
The  Customer Care Specialist acts as the key contact between our customers' and the company and will be responsive to customer's requirements at all times, (both internal and external) and resolve customer queries quickly and will direct their efforts to maximise the customer experience.
We welcome applications from candidates with other European Languages
The role is based in Naas, Ireland and will require full attendance for the training period (4 – 6 weeks) then the role becomes a hybrid role working from the office 3 out of 5 days a week.
This is a 12 month fixed term contract position.
Key responsibilities
Maintain professional, timely and effective communication with our customers
Responsible for all aspects of account administration, account queries and commercial support
Manage customer orders and requests in line with company procedures and propose improvements to procedures and processes, where possible, to improve efficiency and effectiveness
Resolve service issues where possible by clarifying customer complaints, determining cause and seeking solutions and seeking support and escalating appropriately to Lead / Supervisor / Manager
Develop and maintain strong relationships with all customers by effectively managing customer accounts
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of products, customers, processes and suppliers
Build strong relationships with the rest of the supply chain and all departments including the commercial team, work effectively with your Supervisor / Manager to improve the service to the customer
Support the gathering of information to assist the implementation of improvements
Remain fully flexible to meet business requirements and demands
We value courage, ownership, inclusiveness, open-mindedness and an enterprising spirit through success.
Qualifications and skills
In Kerry we understand that people have very different career trajectories and experiences. In order to be successful in this role we would be looking for the right competencies and aptitudes as well as your proven track record.
Fluent French or Polish Speaker
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
The ability to integrate and work effectively with others in a changing environment
High level of attention to detail and strong organisational, analytical, problem solving and administrative skills
A team player
A strong desire for continuous learning and a desire to grow professionally
In Kerry we know that sometimes the perfect candidate doesn’t exist and people can be put off applying for a role if they don’t fit all the requirements. If you are excited about working for us and have the majority of the skills or experience, then please do apply as you could be exactly what we are looking for.

title: Settlements Analyst - Priority Client Services
description:
Overview 

 Susquehanna is a global quantitative trading firm powered by scientific rigor, curiosity, and innovation. Our culture is intellectually driven and highly collaborative, bringing together researchers, engineers, and traders to design and deploy impactful strategies in our systematic trading environment. To meet the unique challenges of global markets, Susquehanna applies machine learning and advanced quantitative research to vast datasets in order to uncover actionable insights and build effective strategies. By uniting deep market expertise with cutting-edge technology, we excel in solving complex problems and pushing boundaries together. 
  
 You will be primarily responsible for Global Settlements for Susquehanna European companies. The role involves working closely with traders in a front office environment. You will be required to build an excellent knowledge of the products traded by Susquehanna and also the international markets in which we operate. 
 This is a superb opportunity for an individual with a keen interest in the financial markets to gain exposure within a true trading environment and further their knowledge. 
  
 What you'll be part of: 
 Ensuring prompt and efficient matching and settlement of all OTC, Client and Exchange Trades across a range of different products such as: Equities, Bonds, ETF’s with a focus on regulatory and economic impact. 
 Manage relationships with Susquehanna clients ensuring a high level of settlement service. 
 Liaison with inter-company departments such as: Securities Lending, Corporate Actions, Technology, Trading Desks and Trade Support to ensure high settlement rate and best service to the traders. 
 Directing the Prime Broker and Direct Market Access (DMA) provider’s settlement functions. 
 Daily monitoring and analysis of all buy-in notices received from Exchanges, Clients and DMA providers. 
 Proactively communicate and build relationships with Sales traders and other relevant parties to quickly and efficiently manage critical trades which may result in settlement risks. 
 Position management through analysis of long/short positions on multi listed securities and instructing reregistration of securities to cover any short positions. 
 Investigation/analysis of all interest claims, fines, buy ins received in order to recommend changes to trading strategies so as to reduce such costs. 
 Develop good relationships with Prime Brokers, Execution Brokers and clients. 
 Compilation and analysis of monthly management reports on trading volume, interest claims, buy-in notices, trade fails and PnL impact. 
 Research and analysis into new markets/products. 
 Participate in strategic initiatives to enhance operational efficiency. 
 Identify and implement process improvements and automation opportunities. 
 Take ownership of new ideas from concept to implementation, helping the firm identify and execute growth opportunities. 
 Project work directly relating to trading desks activities. 
 
 What we're looking for 

 3rd level degree, preferably in a business or finance related discipline is desirable. 
 Experience in a similar role with European & DTC Settlements experience an advantage. 
 Experience in trade matching and using platforms such as CTM and/or Traiana, and knowledge of SSI’s is desirable. 
 A client focus on delivering best service. 
 Aptitude for using technology and improving efficiencies – experience in SQL/Python an advantage. 
 Attention to detail and good organizational skills are essential. 
 Ambitious and self-motivated, not afraid to ask questions and use own initiative. 
 Knowledge of and an interest in financial markets and European Settlements 
 High level of proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel. 
 Strong communicator (verbal and written). 
 Effective problem solving and analytical skills; including effective troubleshooting in a fast paced, time critical environment. 
 Ability to work under pressure and multi-task.

title: Bid Coordinator
description:
Bid Coordinator – Support Role About Your New Employer Join a highly regarded architectural practice , long-established in Dublin and now a trusted partner for some of the world’s largest technology companies.  Leverage over 35 years of experience, with a legacy in designing over seven million square feet of data centres and leading international projects across Ireland, the UK, the Nordics, Germany, Switzerland, and Spain.  Be part of a collaborative team whose expertise extends beyond data centres to commercial, workplace, healthcare, retail, and community architecture—offering a diverse and engaging work culture.
 About Your New Job As the Bid Coordinator, you will coordinate the entire preparation and submission process for both public and private sector tenders, expressions of interest, pre-qualification questionnaires, and other bid submissions.
 Review RFP and tender documents to identify key submission requirements, deadlines, and compliance criteria.
 Efficiently manage inputs from internal and external subject matter experts, consultants, and project partners, ensuring timely and accurate compilation of all documentation.
 You will be responsible for formatting and compiling bid documents to meet RFP standards and company brand guidelines, supporting the creation of technical proposals, presentations, and qualification documents.
 Uphold document control, version management, proofreading, and quality assurance throughout the bidding cycle, and maintain the bid content library and supporting databases.
 What Skills You Need Previous experience in bid coordination, bid support, or a similar administrative or project support role, ideally within architecture, engineering, construction, or related sectors.
 Strong understanding of public and private sector tender processes.
 A relevant third-level degree or equivalent qualification.
 Excellent organisational and coordination abilities to manage multiple deadlines and priorities.
 Demonstrated attention to detail, document quality, and accuracy.
 Confident communicator, both written and verbal, with strong interpersonal skills.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) and Adobe InDesign for professional document production.
 Fluent written and spoken English. German language skills are a plus.
 Proactive, collaborative, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team.
 What's on Offer Opportunity to work with a heritage practice at the forefront of high-profile, international architectural projects.
 Career development, ongoing training, and the chance to shape innovative bid processes and resources.
 Competitive salary of between €40k - 50k tailored to your experience and benefits.
 What's Next Apply now by clicking the “Apply Now" button or get in touch for a confidential discussion about your suitability for this position.
